source.text: Τεκνία μου, ταῦτα γράφω ὑμῖν ἵνα μὴ ἁμάρτητε.

records.literal_gloss: Little children of me, these things I am writing to you so that not you may sin.

en.L: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you may not sin.
en.B: My dear children, I am writing this to you so that you will not sin.
en.R: My dear children, I am writing these things to you so that you will not sin.

fr.L: Mes petits enfants, je vous écris ces choses afin que vous ne péchiez pas.
fr.B: Mes chers enfants, je vous écris ceci pour que vous ne péchiez pas.
fr.R: Mes chers enfants, je vous écris ces choses pour que vous ne commettiez pas de péché.

es.L: Hijitos míos, {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo estas cosas para que no {{plural_you:pequen|pequéis}}.
es.B: Hijitos míos, {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo esto para que no {{plural_you:pequen|pequéis}}.
es.R: Hijos queridos, {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo estas cosas para que no {{plural_you:pequen|pequéis}}.

sw.L: Watoto wangu wadogo, ninawaandikia mambo haya msije mkatenda dhambi.
sw.B: Wanangu wapendwa, nawaandikia haya ili msitende dhambi.
sw.R: Wanangu wapendwa, ninawaandikia mambo haya ili msitende dhambi.

decisions.choice: little children: a loving address from an older leader to all the believers in his care
decisions.reason: Τεκνία is a diminutive of the word for child. The letter uses it, and the similar παιδίον, for the whole community it writes to (2:12, 2:18, 2:28; 3:7, 3:18; 5:21), and Jesus addresses his disciples the same way (John 13:33). It says nothing about their age. The word is neuter and covers women and men alike.

decisions.choice: so that you may not sin: the aim of what he writes is that they not fall into sin at all
alternatives: so that you may stop sinning
decisions.reason: The aorist subjunctive ἁμάρτητε looks at sinning as an act, not a settled way of life. ταῦτα, "these things", points back to 1:5-10. There John said that anyone who claims to have no sin deceives himself (1:8-10); now he guards against the opposite mistake of treating sin as unimportant. The next sentence says what happens when a believer does sin.

decisions.choice: My dear children
decisions.reason: "Little children" now suggests small children; "dear" carries the warmth of the diminutive. Literal keeps "little children". The letter's other word for children (2:14, 2:18) is "children" at every level, so the two Greek words stay distinct at Literal.

decisions.choice: mes petits enfants (L); mes chers enfants (B, R); enfants for the letter's other word (2:14, 2:18) at every level (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in English: "petits enfants" keeps the diminutive at Literal, written without a hyphen, since "petits-enfants" means grandchildren. Balanced and Readable carry its warmth with "chers", and the plain "enfants" keeps the second Greek word apart.

decisions.choice: Hijitos míos (L, B); Hijos queridos (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1 John 5:21 and John 13:33: "Hijitos" is warm, not childish, and Readable says "Hijos queridos", as the English says "dear children". The same for this word through the letter. Every plural "you" is the ustedes / vosotros setting, as in 1:1.

decisions.choice: Watoto wangu wadogo (L); Wanangu wapendwa (B, R)
decisions.reason: A loving address from an older leader to all the believers in his care (m1), as in John 13:33 and 1 John 5:21. Literal keeps "little children"; Balanced and Readable say "my dear children", as the English does. The same words are used for this address through the letter.

source.text: καὶ ἐάν τις ἁμάρτῃ, παράκλητον ἔχομεν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν δίκαιον, καὶ αὐτὸς ἱλασμός ἐστιν περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν, οὐ περὶ τῶν ἡμετέρων δὲ μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ ὅλου τοῦ κόσμου.

records.literal_gloss: And if anyone should sin, an advocate we have toward the Father, Jesus Christ [the] righteous; \v 2 and he [an] atoning-sacrifice is for the sins of us, not for the ours but only, but also for whole the world.

en.L: And if anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} [the] Righteous [One]; \v 2 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} is [the] atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for [the sins of] the whole world.
en.B: Yet if anyone does sin, we have an advocate in the Father's presence, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, who is righteous. \v 2 He {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} is the sacrifice that atones for our sins, and not for ours alone but for the sins of the whole world.
en.R: But if someone does sin, we have an advocate who speaks for us to the Father: Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, who is righteous. \v 2 He {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} is the sacrifice that takes away our sins and puts us right with God. And not only our sins, but the sins of the whole world.

fr.L: Et si quelqu’un pèche, nous avons un défenseur auprès du Père, Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} [le] Juste ; \v 2 et {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} est [le] sacrifice d’expiation pour nos péchés, et non pour les nôtres seulement, mais aussi pour [ceux du] monde entier.
fr.B: Mais si quelqu’un vient à pécher, nous avons un défenseur auprès du Père : Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, qui est juste. \v 2 C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui est le sacrifice d’expiation pour nos péchés, et non seulement pour les nôtres, mais aussi pour ceux du monde entier.
fr.R: Mais si quelqu’un commet un péché, nous avons un défenseur qui parle pour nous au Père : Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, qui est juste. \v 2 C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} le sacrifice qui enlève nos péchés et qui nous réconcilie avec Dieu. Et pas seulement nos péchés, mais aussi les péchés du monde entier.

es.L: Y si alguno peca, tenemos un defensor ante el Padre, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, [el] Justo; \v 2 y {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}} es [el] sacrificio de expiación por nuestros pecados, y no solo por los nuestros, sino también por [los de] todo el mundo.
es.B: Pero si alguno peca, tenemos un defensor ante el Padre: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, que es justo. \v 2 Él mismo es el sacrificio que expía nuestros pecados, y no solo los nuestros, sino también los pecados de todo el mundo.
es.R: Pero si alguien peca, tenemos un defensor que habla por nosotros ante el Padre: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, que es justo. \v 2 Él mismo es el sacrificio que quita nuestros pecados y nos reconcilia con Dios. Y no solo nuestros pecados, sino los pecados de todo el mundo.

sw.L: Na ikiwa mtu yeyote atatenda dhambi, tuna mtetezi kwa Baba: Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, [yule] Mwenye Haki; \v 2 {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ni [dhabihu ya] upatanisho kwa ajili ya dhambi zetu, wala si kwa ajili ya [dhambi] zetu tu, bali pia kwa ajili ya [dhambi za] ulimwengu wote.
sw.B: Lakini mtu yeyote akitenda dhambi, tunaye mtetezi mbele ya Baba, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, aliye mwenye haki. \v 2 Yeye {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ndiye dhabihu inayofanya upatanisho kwa ajili ya dhambi zetu, wala si kwa ajili ya dhambi zetu peke yake, bali kwa ajili ya dhambi za ulimwengu wote.
sw.R: Lakini mtu akitenda dhambi, tunaye mtetezi anayetusemea mbele ya Baba: Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, aliye mwenye haki. \v 2 Yeye {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ndiye dhabihu inayoondoa dhambi zetu na kutupatanisha na Mungu. Wala si dhambi zetu tu, bali pia dhambi za ulimwengu wote.

decisions.choice: if anyone does sin: a particular act of sin that may happen, not a life given over to sin
decisions.reason: The aorist subjunctive ἁμάρτῃ speaks of a sin committed, not of continuing in sin, which the letter treats very differently (3:6-9). John then says "we have", not "you have": he counts himself among those who need the advocate.

decisions.choice: advocate: one who stands beside someone and speaks for them before a judge
decisions.reason: παράκλητος means one called to someone's side, especially to plead their case. Here the setting is a court: the one who has sinned is before the Father, and Jesus speaks for him. In John's Gospel the same word is used four times for the Holy Spirit (John 14:16, 14:26; 15:26; 16:7), and "another" advocate in John 14:16 implies that Jesus himself is the first. The context there is also testimony and judgment (15:26; 16:8-11).

decisions.choice: the righteous one: Jesus is righteous himself, which is why he can plead for those who are not
alternatives: the Righteous One as a title only
decisions.reason: δίκαιον describes Jesus, and the early church also used "the Righteous One" as a name for him (Acts 3:14; 7:52). The point here is that the one who pleads for sinners is himself without sin (3:5, 3:7).

decisions.choice: atoning sacrifice: the offering by which sin is dealt with, so that the broken relationship with God is put right
alternatives: propitiation: the sacrifice that turns away God's anger against sin
expiation: the sacrifice that wipes out or covers sin
decisions.reason: In the Greek Old Testament ἱλασμός is used of the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 25:9), the ram offered to make atonement (Numbers 5:8), a sin offering (Ezekiel 44:27), and the forgiveness found with God (Psalm 130:4). Whether the word looks mainly toward God, turning away his just anger (compare ἱλαστήριον in Romans 3:25, with Romans 1:18), or mainly toward sin, removing it (compare "cleanses us from all sin" in 1:7 and 1:9), has long been discussed. The sacrifice is not a gift by which people win over an unwilling God: in 4:10, God loved us and sent his Son as ἱλασμὸν for our sins. "Atoning sacrifice" keeps both sides in view; a footnote gives the other renderings.

decisions.choice: the whole world: all people everywhere, not only the believers John writes to
alternatives: the world as the system opposed to God (as in 2:15-17)
decisions.reason: Here "world" means humankind, as in John 1:29 ("the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world"), 3:16 and 4:42 ("the Savior of the world"). The sentence says how far the sacrifice reaches; it does not say that everyone is in fact forgiven, which the letter ties to confessing sins (1:9) and to believing in the Son (5:10-12).

decisions.choice: for the sins of the whole world: the noun "sins" is understood from the first half
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "not for ours only but also for the whole world", leaving "sins" to be supplied from "our sins".

decisions.choice: an advocate (lowercase)
alternatives: someone who speaks to the Father in our defense
decisions.reason: The same English word as in John's Gospel, where "the Advocate" is a title for the Spirit, so the link stays visible. Here the word has no article and describes what Jesus does rather than naming him, so it is not capitalized. Readable adds "who speaks for us" to say what an advocate does.

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R); {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}
decisions.reason: Title setting for Christ; the deity_pronoun setting for the pronouns that refer to him. "He" at the start of a sentence needs no span.

decisions.choice: the sacrifice that takes away our sins and puts us right with God
alternatives: the atoning sacrifice for our sins
decisions.reason: "Atone" and "propitiation" are hard words for young readers. Readable names both sides of meaning decision m4: sin is taken away (the language of John 1:29) and the relationship with God is put right. It goes further than the one Greek word, so reviewers may prefer the plainer "the sacrifice for our sins".

decisions.choice: the sins of the whole world
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "the sins of" (meaning decision m6); Literal puts it in brackets.

decisions.choice: un défenseur, lowercase, at every level
decisions.reason: The same word as "le Défenseur", the French title of the Spirit in John 14-16, so the link stays visible; here it has no article and says what Jesus does (m2), so it is lowercase, as in English. "Avocat" would sound like a lawyer paid for a case.

decisions.choice: sacrifice d’expiation (L, B); le sacrifice qui enlève nos péchés et qui nous réconcilie avec Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: "Propitiation" is no longer understood, and "victime" today suggests someone who suffers harm. "Sacrifice d’expiation" names the offering by which sin is dealt with (m4); Readable says both sides of it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: un defensor (lowercase)
decisions.reason: The same word that Spanish John renders "Defensor" for the Spirit (John 14:16): one who stands beside someone and speaks for them before a judge (meaning decision m2). Here it is not a title, so it is lowercase, as in the English; "abogado" sounds like the modern profession.

decisions.choice: sacrificio de expiación (L); sacrificio que expía (B); sacrificio que quita nuestros pecados y nos reconcilia con Dios (R)
decisions.reason: As in Romans 3:25 and Hebrews 2:17, Spanish uses "expiación" for the sacrifice that deals with sin and puts right the broken relationship with God (meaning decision m4); "propiciación" is little known today. Readable says both halves plainly, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: mtetezi (lowercase)
decisions.reason: The word is one who stands beside someone and speaks for them before a judge (m2). "Mtetezi" (defender, advocate) is the word used for the Spirit in John 14:16, so the link John makes between the two advocates stays visible; it is lowercase here, as the English "advocate" is.

decisions.choice: [dhabihu ya] upatanisho (L); dhabihu inayofanya upatanisho (B); dhabihu inayoondoa dhambi zetu na kutupatanisha na Mungu (R)
decisions.reason: The offering by which sin is dealt with and the relationship with God put right (m4). "Upatanisho" is the word used in Romans 3:25 and Hebrews 2:17; Swahili needs "dhabihu" (sacrifice) beside it to say that Jesus himself is the offering, bracketed at Literal. Readable spells it out, as the English Readable does.

source.text: Καὶ ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν ὅτι ἐγνώκαμεν αὐτόν, ἐὰν τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ τηρῶμεν.

records.literal_gloss: And by this we know that we have come to know him, if the commandments of him we keep.

en.L: And in this we know that we have come to know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: if we keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands.
en.B: We can be sure that we have come to know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in this way: if we keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands.
en.R: We can be sure that we know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} if we obey what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commands.

fr.L: Et en ceci nous savons que nous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avons connu : si nous gardons {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements.
fr.B: Voici comment nous pouvons être sûrs de {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avoir connu : si nous gardons {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements.
fr.R: Nous pouvons être sûrs que nous {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} connaissons si nous obéissons à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} commande.

es.L: Y en esto sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} hemos conocido: si guardamos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos.
es.B: Podemos estar seguros de que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} hemos llegado a conocer en esto: si guardamos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos.
es.R: Podemos estar seguros de que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} conocemos si obedecemos lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} manda.

sw.L: Na hivi ndivyo tunavyojua kwamba tumekuja kumjua: ikiwa tunashika amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.B: Tunaweza kuwa na hakika kwamba tumemjua kwa njia hii: tukizishika amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.R: Tunaweza kuwa na hakika kwamba tunamjua tukitii amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.

decisions.choice: by this ... if: the test John means is the condition that follows
decisions.reason: "By this we know" is one of the letter's set phrases (2:5; 3:16, 3:19, 3:24; 4:2, 4:13; 5:2). Here τούτῳ points forward to the clause with ἐὰν: keeping his commands is the evidence that we know him.

decisions.choice: we have come to know him: a knowledge that began and continues
decisions.reason: The perfect ἐγνώκαμεν describes a knowing that started and still holds. It is personal knowledge of God, not information about him. The next verse suggests that some people claimed to know God while ignoring his commands.

decisions.choice: him: most likely God, though the letter does not always keep God and Christ apart
decisions.reason: The last person named is Jesus Christ (2:1-2), but "the love of God" in 2:5 suggests God is meant, and in this letter keeping God's commands means believing in his Son and loving one another (3:23). The translation keeps "him" so that the reader can weigh both.

decisions.choice: commands: what God has told his people to do
decisions.reason: In this letter the commands are summed up as believing in the name of his Son Jesus Christ and loving one another (3:23).

decisions.choice: keep his commands (L, B); obey what he commands (R)
decisions.reason: "Commands", as in John 10:18: "commandments" now suggests the Ten Commandments in particular. Readable says "obey", the everyday word for keeping a command.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Pronouns for God or Christ take the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: commandements (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: The English says "commands" because "commandments" now suggests the Ten Commandments. French "commandement" has no such narrow sense and is the ordinary word for what God tells his people to do (m4), as in 2 John; "ordres" would sound military. Readable says "obéir à ce qu’il commande".

decisions.choice: guardar sus mandamientos (L, B); obedecer lo que él manda (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1 John 5:2-3: "mandamientos" and "guardar" at Literal and Balanced, plain "obedecer" at Readable.

decisions.choice: kuzishika amri (L, B); kutii amri (R)
decisions.reason: As in John 14:15 and 1 John 5:3: "kushika" (keep) for keeping commandments, and Readable says "kutii" (obey), as the English Readable does. "Amri" is the word for command through the letter (m4).

source.text: ὁ λέγων ὅτι Ἔγνωκα αὐτὸν καὶ τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ μὴ τηρῶν ψεύστης ἐστίν, καὶ ἐν τούτῳ ἡ ἀλήθεια οὐκ ἔστιν·

records.literal_gloss: The [one] saying, "I have known him," and the commandments of him not keeping a liar is, and in this [one] the truth not is;

en.L: The one saying, "I have come to know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}," and not keeping {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands is a liar, and in {{gender:that person|that man}} the truth is not.
en.B: Anyone who says, "I have come to know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}," but does not keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands is a liar, and the truth is not in {{gender:them|him}}.
en.R: Suppose someone says, "I know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}," but does not obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands. That person is a liar, and the truth is not in {{gender:them|him}}.

fr.L: Celui qui dit : « Je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ai connu » et qui ne garde pas {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements est un menteur, et en celui-là la vérité n’est pas.
fr.B: Celui qui dit : « Je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ai connu », mais ne garde pas {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements, est un menteur, et la vérité n’est pas en lui.
fr.R: Imaginons que quelqu’un dise : « Je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} connais », mais qu’il n’obéisse pas à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements. Celui-là est un menteur, et la vérité n’est pas en lui.

es.L: El que dice: «Yo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} he conocido», y no guarda {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos, es mentiroso, y en {{gender:esa persona|ese hombre}} la verdad no está.
es.B: Quien dice: «Yo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} he llegado a conocer», pero no guarda {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos, es un mentiroso, y la verdad no está en {{gender:esa persona|él}}.
es.R: Supongamos que alguien dice: «Yo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} conozco», pero no obedece {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandatos. Esa persona es mentirosa, y la verdad no está en ella.

sw.L: Mtu anayesema, "Nimekuja kumjua," bila kushika amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, ni mwongo, na ndani ya mtu huyo kweli haiko.
sw.B: Yeyote anayesema, "Nimemjua," lakini hashiki amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, ni mwongo; kweli haipo ndani yake.
sw.R: Huenda mtu akasema, "Ninamjua," lakini hatii amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Mtu huyo ni mwongo, na kweli haimo ndani yake.

decisions.choice: anyone who says: a general case, which may have real people in view
decisions.reason: This is the first of three sayings that begin "the one who says" (2:4, 2:6, 2:9), following the three "if we say" sayings of 1:6, 1:8 and 1:10. The form is general, but the claims are the kind made by those who later left the church (2:19). ὅτι introduces the claim in the speaker's own words.

decisions.choice: the truth is not in him: God's truth has no hold on that person's life
alternatives: he is not telling the truth
decisions.reason: In John, "truth" is the reality of God made known in Jesus (John 14:6), something a person lives in, not only a set of correct statements. 1:8 uses the same expression. Saying one knows God while ignoring what he commands shows that his truth has not taken root.

decisions.choice: {{gender:that person|that man}} (L); {{gender:them|him}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The claim could be made by a man or a woman, so the gender setting applies. Readable says "That person", which needs no span.

decisions.choice: Suppose someone says ... That person is a liar
alternatives: Anyone who says ... is a liar
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long subject into two sentences.

decisions.choice: celui qui … celui-là, lui, with no gender span (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:that person|that man}} and {{gender:them|him}} for anyone who makes the claim. French "celui qui", "quelqu’un" and "quiconque" already mean anyone, and the "il", "lui" and "celui-là" that refer back to them are ordinary generic French, so no span is added (style guide 7), here and through the letter.

decisions.choice: {{gender:esa persona|ese hombre}} (L); {{gender:esa persona|él}} (B); ella, no span (R)
decisions.reason: The English gender spans are kept where Spanish has a pronoun that marks a man. Where Spanish already says "esa persona" or uses a form that does not mark gender ("le", "sus ojos", "no sabe adónde va"), no span is needed. The same through this chapter.

decisions.choice: huyo, mtu, ndani yake, no gender span
decisions.reason: The case is general, any person (m1). "Mtu", "huyo" and "yake" say nothing about sex, so Swahili has no counterpart to the English spans "that person|that man" and "them|him", here or elsewhere in the chapter.

source.text: ὃς δ’ ἂν τηρῇ αὐτοῦ τὸν λόγον, ἀληθῶς ἐν τούτῳ ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ τετελείωται.

records.literal_gloss: But whoever keeps of him the word, truly in this [one] the love of God has been completed.

en.L: But whoever keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word, truly in this [one] the love of God has been made complete.
en.B: But whoever keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word, in that person the love of God has truly reached its goal.
en.R: But if anyone obeys {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word, God's love has really done its full work in {{gender:them|him}}.

fr.L: Mais quiconque garde {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} parole, vraiment en celui-là l’amour de Dieu a été rendu complet.
fr.B: Mais celui qui garde {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} parole, en lui l’amour de Dieu a vraiment atteint son but.
fr.R: Mais si quelqu’un obéit à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} parole, l’amour de Dieu a vraiment accompli en lui toute son œuvre.

es.L: Pero el que guarda {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} palabra, verdaderamente en este el amor de Dios ha sido completado.
es.B: Pero quien guarda {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} palabra, en esa persona el amor de Dios ha alcanzado de verdad su meta.
es.R: Pero si alguien obedece {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} palabra, el amor de Dios ha hecho de verdad toda su obra en {{gender:esa persona|él}}.

sw.L: Lakini yeyote anayelishika neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, kwa kweli ndani ya mtu huyo upendo wa Mungu umekamilishwa.
sw.B: Lakini yeyote anayelishika neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, ndani yake upendo wa Mungu umefikia lengo lake kwa kweli.
sw.R: Lakini mtu akilitii neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, upendo wa Mungu umefanya kazi yake kikamilifu ndani yake.

decisions.choice: his word: everything God has said, the message they heard from the beginning
decisions.reason: "His word" stands in place of "his commands" (2:4) and is wider: it is God's whole message, which they heard from the start (2:7, 2:24).

decisions.choice: the love of God: most likely God's own love, which reaches its goal in the one who obeys
alternatives: love for God, shown in obedience
the kind of love that comes from God
decisions.reason: The Greek "love of God" can mean God's love or love for God. The letter uses the phrase in both directions (love for God in 5:3; God's love in 4:9). Here the verb says the love is brought to completion, as God's love is in 4:12, so God's love for us, working itself out in those who keep his word, is the more likely sense. Love for God, shown by keeping his word (5:3), remains possible.

decisions.choice: has been completed: has reached its goal, not that the person has become morally perfect
decisions.reason: τελειόω means to bring to completion. The letter uses it again for love in 4:12, 4:17 and 4:18. It speaks of love achieving what it was meant to achieve, not of a sinless life (1:8).

decisions.choice: has truly reached its goal (B); has really done its full work (R)
decisions.reason: "Perfected" suggests flawlessness (meaning decision m3). Literal says "made complete".

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: Anyone, man or woman, is meant. Balanced says "that person", which needs no span.

decisions.choice: ha alcanzado su meta (B); ha hecho toda su obra (R)
decisions.reason: "Perfeccionarse" would suggest that the person has become morally perfect, which meaning decision m3 rules out. "Su" here is the love's own goal, not a pronoun for God.

decisions.choice: upendo; kupenda
decisions.reason: As in John's Gospel: "upendo" is the noun for love through the letter, and "kupenda" the verb. "Mapenzi" is kept for God's will (2:17, 5:14), and in everyday speech often means romantic love.

decisions.choice: umekamilishwa (L); umefikia lengo lake (B); umefanya kazi yake kikamilifu (R)
decisions.reason: The love has reached its goal; the person is not said to be morally perfect (m3). "Umekamilishwa" (has been made complete) keeps the passive at Literal, and Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the English does. "Mkamilifu" (perfect) would suggest a flawless person.

source.text: ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ ἐσμεν·

records.literal_gloss: By this we know that in him we are;

en.L: By this we know that we are in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: That is how we know we are in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: That is how we know we are joined to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: À ceci nous savons que nous sommes en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: C’est ainsi que nous savons que nous sommes en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Voilà comment nous savons que nous sommes unis à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

es.L: En esto sabemos que estamos en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Así es como sabemos que estamos en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Así es como sabemos que estamos unidos a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

sw.L: Kwa hili tunajua kwamba tuko ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Hivyo ndivyo tunavyojua kwamba tuko ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Hivyo ndivyo tunavyojua kwamba tumeunganishwa {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.

decisions.choice: by this: points back to keeping his word (2:5a)
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in the letter τούτῳ often points forward to a clause that follows (2:3). Here no such clause follows inside the sentence, so it most naturally sums up what has just been said: keeping his word is how we know.

decisions.choice: in him: sharing a common life with God, as branches are in the vine
decisions.reason: Being "in him" is the union Jesus describes in John 15:4-7 and 17:21. 2:6 calls it "remaining in him".

decisions.choice: That is how
decisions.reason: "That" signals that the phrase points back (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: joined to him
decisions.reason: "In him" says little to young readers; "joined to" gives the sense of meaning decision m2.

source.text: ὁ λέγων ἐν αὐτῷ μένειν ὀφείλει καθὼς ἐκεῖνος περιεπάτησεν καὶ αὐτὸς περιπατεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] claiming in him to remain ought just as that [one] walked also himself to walk.

en.L: The one claiming to remain in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} ought {{gender:themselves|himself}} also to walk just as that [one] walked.
en.B: Anyone who claims to remain in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} ought to live in the same way that Jesus lived.
en.R: Anyone who says, "I remain in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}," should live the way Jesus lived.

fr.L: Celui qui dit demeurer en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} doit, lui aussi, marcher comme celui-là a marché.
fr.B: Celui qui prétend demeurer en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} doit vivre de la même manière que Jésus a vécu.
fr.R: Si quelqu’un dit : « Je demeure en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} », il doit vivre comme Jésus a vécu.

es.L: El que dice que permanece en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} debe también andar así como anduvo aquel.
es.B: Quien afirma que permanece en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} debe vivir de la misma manera que vivió Jesús.
es.R: Quien dice: «Yo permanezco en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}», debe vivir como vivió Jesús.

sw.L: Yule anayesema kwamba anakaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} anapaswa yeye mwenyewe pia kutembea kama vile yule alivyotembea.
sw.B: Yeyote anayedai kwamba anakaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} anapaswa kuishi kama Yesu alivyoishi.
sw.R: Yeyote anayesema, "Ninakaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}," anapaswa kuishi jinsi Yesu alivyoishi.

decisions.choice: remain: stay joined to him in a lasting way
decisions.reason: μένω is one of John's key words. It is used for staying in a place (John 1:38-39) and for the lasting union between Jesus and those who are his (John 6:56; 15:4-10). It comes again and again in this chapter (2:10, 2:14, 2:17, 2:19, 2:24, 2:27, 2:28).

decisions.choice: that one: Jesus
decisions.reason: The letter uses ἐκεῖνος as a way of pointing to Jesus (3:3, 3:5, 3:7, 3:16; 4:17). "Walked" in the past tense also points to his life on earth.

decisions.choice: walk: live, conduct one's life
decisions.reason: To walk is a Hebrew way of speaking about how one lives, used already in 1:6-7.

decisions.choice: remain
decisions.reason: As in John's Gospel: "remain" for this verb in its weighty sense, not the older "abide". "Live in" would blur it with "walk" in the same verse.

decisions.choice: the same way that Jesus lived
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus (meaning decision m2) and say "live" for the idiom "walk" (m3). Literal keeps "walk" and "that [one]".

decisions.choice: {{gender:themselves|himself}}
decisions.reason: The one who makes the claim may be a man or a woman.

decisions.choice: demeurer at every level (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in John and 2 John: "demeurer" for this verb in its weighty sense (m1), so that 2:6, 2:24-28, 3:24 and 4:12-16 read alike; the English keeps "remain" at every level. Where the verb means simply staying with people (2:19), Balanced and Readable say "rester".

decisions.choice: permanecer
decisions.reason: As in John 15, the verb is "permanecer" at every level throughout the letter. In Literal, Spanish says "debe también andar" with no pronoun, so the English span "themselves|himself" has no counterpart.

decisions.choice: kukaa ndani yake
decisions.reason: As in John 15: "kukaa" for this verb throughout the letter, so that "remain" stays one word for the reader (m1), as the English keeps "remain".

decisions.choice: yule, no span
decisions.reason: The Greek points to Jesus with "that one" (m2). Literal keeps the demonstrative "yule", which, like the English "that [one]", takes no deity_pronoun span; Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

source.text: Ἀγαπητοί, οὐκ ἐντολὴν καινὴν γράφω ὑμῖν, ἀλλ’ ἐντολὴν παλαιὰν ἣν εἴχετε ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς· ἡ ἐντολὴ ἡ παλαιά ἐστιν ὁ λόγος ὃν ἠκούσατε.

records.literal_gloss: Beloved, not a commandment new I am writing to you, but a commandment old which you had from [the] beginning; the commandment the old is the word which you heard.

en.L: Beloved, I am not writing a new command to you, but an old command, which you have had from [the] beginning. The old command is the word that you heard.
en.B: Dear friends, what I am writing to you is not a new command but an old one, one you have had from the beginning. That old command is the word you heard.
en.R: Dear friends, I am not writing to give you a new command. It is an old command, one you have had from the very beginning. This old command is the message you already heard.

fr.L: Bien-aimés, ce n’est pas un commandement nouveau que je vous écris, mais un commandement ancien, que vous aviez depuis le commencement. Le commandement ancien est la parole que vous avez entendue.
fr.B: Chers amis, ce que je vous écris n’est pas un commandement nouveau, mais un commandement ancien, celui que vous avez depuis le commencement. Ce commandement ancien, c’est la parole que vous avez entendue.
fr.R: Chers amis, je ne vous écris pas pour vous donner un commandement nouveau. C’est un commandement ancien, que vous avez depuis le tout début. Ce commandement ancien, c’est le message que vous avez déjà entendu.

es.L: Amados, no {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo un mandamiento nuevo, sino un mandamiento antiguo, que {{plural_you:tenían|teníais}} desde [el] principio. El mandamiento antiguo es la palabra que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}}.
es.B: Queridos amigos, lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo no es un mandamiento nuevo, sino uno antiguo, el que {{plural_you:han|habéis}} tenido desde el principio. Ese mandamiento antiguo es la palabra que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}}.
es.R: Queridos amigos, no {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo para {{plural_you:darles|daros}} un mandamiento nuevo. Es un mandamiento antiguo, uno que {{plural_you:han|habéis}} tenido desde el mismo principio. Este mandamiento antiguo es el mensaje que ya {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}}.

sw.L: Wapendwa, si amri mpya ninayowaandikia, bali amri ya zamani, ambayo mmekuwa nayo tangu mwanzo. Amri hiyo ya zamani ni neno mlilosikia.
sw.B: Rafiki zangu wapendwa, ninachowaandikia si amri mpya, bali ni ya zamani, ile mliyokuwa nayo tangu mwanzo. Amri hiyo ya zamani ni lile neno mlilosikia.
sw.R: Rafiki zangu wapendwa, siwaandikii ili kuwapa amri mpya. Ni amri ya zamani, mliyokuwa nayo tangu mwanzo kabisa. Amri hiyo ya zamani ni ule ujumbe mliokwisha kuusikia.

decisions.choice: beloved: people John loves, and whom God loves
decisions.reason: Ἀγαπητοί is a warm address to all the readers, used again in 3:2, 3:21; 4:1, 4:7, 4:11. It comes just before the command to love.

decisions.choice: from the beginning: since they first heard the message about Jesus
alternatives: from the beginning of creation (as in 1:1)
decisions.reason: The phrase is tied to what they "heard" (2:24; 3:11; 2 John 5-6): the command was part of the gospel from the day it reached them. It is old to them, not something the false teachers have newly brought.

decisions.choice: the command: to love one another
decisions.reason: The command is not named here, but 2:9-11 speaks of loving one's brother, and 3:11 and 3:23 give it in full: "that we should love one another". Jesus gave it to his disciples in John 13:34.

decisions.choice: the word: the message they heard
alternatives: the Word, Christ himself (as in John 1:1)
decisions.reason: Here "word" is what they heard, the message (1:5 uses a related noun), not the title of Christ.

decisions.choice: Dear friends
decisions.reason: "Beloved" is now rare outside church language. Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: message
decisions.reason: Readable says "message" to show that the word is what they heard (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: Bien-aimés (L); Chers amis (B, R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in English: "bien-aimés" is now church language, kept at Literal; Balanced and Readable use the warm address of a French letter.

decisions.choice: Amados (L); Queridos amigos (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English, and as Philippians 4:1 says "queridos amigos" at Readable.

decisions.choice: Wapendwa (L); Rafiki zangu wapendwa (B, R)
decisions.reason: People John loves and whom God loves (m1). Literal keeps the one word, as 1 Peter and Jude do; Balanced and Readable say "my dear friends", as the English "Dear friends" and 1 Corinthians 10:14 do.

source.text: πάλιν ἐντολὴν καινὴν γράφω ὑμῖν, ὅ ἐστιν ἀληθὲς ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν, ὅτι ἡ σκοτία παράγεται καὶ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν ἤδη φαίνει.

records.literal_gloss: Again a commandment new I am writing to you, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the light the true already shines.

en.L: Again, I am writing a new command to you, which is true in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light already shines.
en.B: And yet the command I am writing to you is a new one. Its newness is real in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and in you, for the darkness is passing away, and already the true light is shining.
en.R: And yet what I am writing to you is a new command too. You can see that it is new in Jesus and in you, because the darkness is going away and the true light is already shining.

fr.L: De nouveau, c’est un commandement nouveau que je vous écris, ce qui est vrai en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et en vous, parce que les ténèbres passent et que la vraie lumière brille déjà.
fr.B: Et pourtant, le commandement que je vous écris est nouveau. Sa nouveauté est réelle en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et en vous, car les ténèbres s’en vont et la vraie lumière brille déjà.
fr.R: Et pourtant, ce que je vous écris est aussi un commandement nouveau. Vous pouvez voir qu’il est nouveau en Jésus et en vous, parce que les ténèbres disparaissent et que la vraie lumière brille déjà.

es.L: Por otra parte, {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo un mandamiento nuevo, lo cual es verdad en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque la oscuridad va pasando y la luz verdadera ya brilla.
es.B: Y sin embargo, el mandamiento que {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo es nuevo. Su novedad es real en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque la oscuridad va pasando, y ya brilla la luz verdadera.
es.R: Y sin embargo, lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo es también un mandamiento nuevo. {{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} ver que es nuevo en Jesús y en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque la oscuridad se está yendo y la luz verdadera ya está brillando.

sw.L: Kwa upande mwingine, ninawaandikia amri mpya, jambo ambalo ni la kweli ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na ndani yenu, kwa kuwa giza linapita, na nuru ya kweli inang'aa tayari.
sw.B: Hata hivyo, amri ninayowaandikia ni mpya. Upya wake ni kweli ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na ndani yenu, kwa maana giza linapita, na tayari nuru ya kweli inang'aa.
sw.R: Hata hivyo, ninachowaandikia ni amri mpya pia. Mnaweza kuona kwamba ni mpya ndani ya Yesu na ndani yenu, kwa sababu giza linaondoka, na nuru ya kweli tayari inang'aa.

decisions.choice: again: here "on the other hand", a second way of looking at the same command
decisions.reason: πάλιν does not introduce a second command. It is the same command of love, old because they have always had it, and new for the reason the sentence goes on to give.

decisions.choice: which is true: what is true is that the command is new
decisions.reason: ὅ is neuter, while ἐντολή is feminine, so the relative does not refer to the command but to the whole statement that it is new. Its newness is real in Christ and in the believers.

decisions.choice: in him: in Christ, who lived out the command of love completely
decisions.reason: Jesus called it "a new command" in John 13:34 and gave its measure: "as I have loved you". The newness was first seen in him, and is now seen in those who love one another.

decisions.choice: because: gives the reason the command is new
decisions.reason: The new age has begun: the darkness is on its way out and the true light is already shining, so the old command now belongs to a new time. Taking ὅτι as "that" would make the passing darkness the content of what is true; the sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: the darkness is passing away and the true light already shines
decisions.reason: John 1:5 and 1:9 speak of the light shining in the darkness and of "the true light" coming into the world, and Jesus calls himself the light of the world (John 8:12). The present tense παράγεται says the darkness is in the middle of passing; the same verb is used of the world in 2:17.

decisions.choice: in Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Its newness is real
decisions.reason: Balanced makes plain what is true (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Kwa upande mwingine (L); Hata hivyo (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Again" here means "on the other hand", a second way of looking at the same command (m1). "Tena" (again) would suggest a second, different command, so Literal says "kwa upande mwingine" (on the other hand), and Balanced and Readable say "hata hivyo" (and yet), as the English does.

source.text: ὁ λέγων ἐν τῷ φωτὶ εἶναι καὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ μισῶν ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ ἐστὶν ἕως ἄρτι.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] claiming in the light to be and the brother of him hating in the darkness is until now.

en.L: The one claiming to be in the light and hating {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}} is in the darkness until now.
en.B: Someone who says they are in the light, and yet hates {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}}, is in the darkness even now.
en.R: Someone may say, "I am in the light," and still hate a fellow believer. That person is still in the darkness.

fr.L: Celui qui dit être dans la lumière et qui hait {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}} est dans les ténèbres jusqu’à maintenant.
fr.B: Celui qui dit être dans la lumière tout en haïssant {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}} est encore dans les ténèbres.
fr.R: Quelqu’un peut dire : « Je suis dans la lumière », et pourtant haïr un frère ou une sœur dans la foi. Celui-là est encore dans les ténèbres.

es.L: El que dice estar en la luz y odia a {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}} está en la oscuridad hasta ahora.
es.B: Quien dice que está en la luz, pero odia a {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}}, sigue todavía en la oscuridad.
es.R: Alguien puede decir: «Estoy en la luz», y aun así odiar a {{gender:un hermano o una hermana en la fe|un hermano en la fe}}. Esa persona sigue en la oscuridad.

sw.L: Yule anayedai kuwa katika nuru na kumchukia ndugu yake yumo gizani mpaka sasa.
sw.B: Mtu anaweza kusema kwamba yuko katika nuru, lakini kama anamchukia ndugu yake, bado yuko gizani hata sasa.
sw.R: Huenda mtu akasema, "Niko katika nuru," lakini bado anamchukia mwamini mwenzake. Mtu huyo bado yuko gizani.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow believer, man or woman
decisions.reason: In this letter ἀδελφός means a member of the Christian family (3:14-17; 4:20-21; 5:16), not a sibling. The masculine form was the ordinary way to speak of men and women together.

decisions.choice: hates: refuses to love
decisions.reason: John allows no middle ground between loving and hating (2:10-11; 3:14-15). Not loving a fellow believer is already hating him.

decisions.choice: in the light / in the darkness: living in fellowship with God, or apart from him
decisions.reason: God is light (1:5); to walk in the light is to live in fellowship with him and with one another (1:6-7).

decisions.choice: {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}}
decisions.reason: The gender setting, since a fellow believer of either sex is meant. In Balanced, "they" for "someone" is already inclusive and needs no span.

decisions.choice: a fellow believer
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that a member of the church is meant (meaning decision m1); the phrase is already inclusive, so it needs no span.

decisions.choice: {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}} (L, B); un frère ou une sœur dans la foi (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: A fellow believer of either sex is meant (m1). French "un autre croyant" is masculine, so Readable says "un frère ou une sœur dans la foi", which is already inclusive and needs no span. Literal and Balanced keep the noun under the setting, and the generic "il", "lui" that follow take none.

decisions.choice: {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}}
decisions.reason: As in 1 John 5:16: the plural "hermanos" covers men and women, but the singular "su hermano" names a man, and John means any fellow believer (meaning decision m1), so it takes the gender setting. The same in verses 10-11.

decisions.choice: ndugu yake (L, B); mwamini mwenzake (R); no gender span
alternatives: ndugu yake wa kiume au wa kike
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brother or sister, a fellow believer of either sex (m1), so the English span "their brother or sister|his brother" has no Swahili counterpart, here or in verses 10-11. Readable says "mwamini mwenzake" (a fellow believer), as 5:16 and the English Readable do.

source.text: ὁ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ φωτὶ μένει, καὶ σκάνδαλον ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν·

records.literal_gloss: The [one] loving the brother of him in the light remains, and a stumbling-block in him not there is;

en.L: The one loving {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}} remains in the light, and there is no cause of stumbling in {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: Whoever loves {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}} remains in the light, and in {{gender:them|him}} there is nothing that causes stumbling.
en.R: Anyone who loves a fellow believer remains in the light, and nothing will make {{gender:them|him}} stumble.

fr.L: Celui qui aime {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}} demeure dans la lumière, et il n’y a pas en lui d’occasion de chute.
fr.B: Celui qui aime {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}} demeure dans la lumière, et il n’y a rien en lui qui fasse trébucher.
fr.R: Celui qui aime un frère ou une sœur dans la foi demeure dans la lumière, et rien ne le fera trébucher.

es.L: El que ama a {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}} permanece en la luz, y no hay tropiezo en {{gender:esa persona|él}}.
es.B: Quien ama a {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}} permanece en la luz, y en {{gender:esa persona|él}} no hay nada que haga tropezar.
es.R: Quien ama a {{gender:un hermano o una hermana en la fe|un hermano en la fe}} permanece en la luz, y nada {{gender:hará tropezar a esa persona|lo hará tropezar}}.

sw.L: Anayempenda ndugu yake anakaa katika nuru, na hakuna kikwazo ndani yake.
sw.B: Yeyote anayempenda ndugu yake anakaa katika nuru, na ndani yake hamna kitu kinachosababisha kujikwaa.
sw.R: Yeyote anayempenda mwamini mwenzake anakaa katika nuru, na hakuna kitu kitakachomfanya ajikwae.

decisions.choice: remains in the light: goes on living in fellowship with God
decisions.reason: The verb is John's "remain" (2:6). The one who loves is not only in the light for a moment but stays there.

decisions.choice: nothing that causes stumbling: nothing that makes that person fall into sin
alternatives: nothing in that person that makes others stumble
nothing in the light to trip over
decisions.reason: σκάνδαλον is a snag or trap that makes someone fall. Since 2:11 says the one who hates walks in darkness and cannot see where he is going, the contrast is most likely that the one who loves walks without tripping (compare John 11:9-10). It could also mean that such a person gives others no cause to fall, or, if αὐτῷ is taken as "it", that there is nothing in the light to trip over.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}}; {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: A fellow believer of either sex, and a person of either sex who loves, is meant. Readable says "a fellow believer" as in 2:9.

decisions.choice: no cause of stumbling in them (L); nothing that causes stumbling (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the open wording of the Greek; Readable follows meaning decision m2.

en.L: But the one hating {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}} is in the darkness and walks in the darkness, and does not know where {{gender:they are|he is}} going, because the darkness has blinded {{gender:their|his}} eyes.
en.B: But whoever hates {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}} is in the darkness and goes about in it, not knowing where {{gender:they are|he is}} headed, because the darkness has blinded {{gender:their|his}} eyes.

fr.L: Mais celui qui hait {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}} est dans les ténèbres et marche dans les ténèbres, et il ne sait pas où il va, parce que les ténèbres ont aveuglé ses yeux.
fr.B: Mais celui qui hait {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}} est dans les ténèbres et y marche ; il ne sait pas où il va, parce que les ténèbres lui ont aveuglé les yeux.

sw.B: Lakini yeyote anayemchukia ndugu yake yuko gizani na anatembea humo, bila kujua anakoelekea, kwa sababu giza limeyapofusha macho yake.

decisions.choice: walking in darkness, not knowing where one is going, blinded
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the same picture in John 12:35: whoever walks in the darkness does not know where he is going. John 12:40 quotes Isaiah 6:10 on eyes that God has blinded. Here it is the darkness itself, chosen through hatred, that blinds.

decisions.choice: has blinded: the darkness has done its work, and the person is now blind
alternatives: blinded at some time in the past
decisions.reason: The aorist ἐτύφλωσεν states the fact; with "is in the darkness" and "walks" in the present, the result still holds.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}}; {{gender:they are|he is}}; {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: Hatred of a fellow believer by a man or a woman is meant, so the gender setting applies to each pronoun. Readable says "a fellow believer" as in 2:9.

source.text: Γράφω ὑμῖν, τεκνία, ὅτι ἀφέωνται ὑμῖν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι διὰ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: I am writing to you, little children, because have been forgiven you the sins because of the name of him;

en.L: I am writing to you, little children, because [your] sins have been forgiven you on account of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.B: Dear children, I am writing to you because your sins stand forgiven for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.R: Dear children, I am writing to you because God has forgiven your sins for the sake of Jesus.

fr.L: Je vous écris, petits enfants, parce que les péchés vous ont été pardonnés à cause de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.
fr.B: Mes chers enfants, je vous écris parce que vos péchés vous sont pardonnés à cause de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.
fr.R: Mes chers enfants, je vous écris parce que Dieu vous a pardonné vos péchés grâce à Jésus.

es.L: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} escribo, hijitos, porque {{plural_you:se les han|se os han}} perdonado los pecados por causa de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.
es.B: Hijitos, {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo porque {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pecados están perdonados por causa de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.
es.R: Hijos queridos, {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo porque Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} ha perdonado los pecados por causa de Jesús.

sw.L: Ninawaandikia, watoto wadogo, kwa kuwa mmesamehewa dhambi [zenu] kwa sababu ya jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.

sw.R: Wanangu wapendwa, nawaandikia kwa sababu Mungu amewasamehe dhambi zenu kwa ajili ya Yesu.

decisions.choice: because: each address gives the reason John writes
alternatives: that: each address gives what he writes
decisions.reason: ὅτι can mean "because" or "that". Read as "because", John writes to them since these things are already true of them; read as "that", he is assuring them of these things. The six sayings of 2:12-14 have the same form and are best read the same way. Both readings fit the warm tone; "because" suits the reasons he gives in 2:21.

decisions.choice: three addresses: all the readers as children, then two groups within them, the older (fathers) and the younger (young men)
alternatives: three groups by age: children, older men, young men
three stages of growth in faith
decisions.reason: The letter uses τεκνίον and παιδίον for all its readers (2:1, 2:18, 2:28), and what is said of the children here, forgiveness and knowing the Father, is true of every believer. So the children are most likely the whole church, and fathers and young men two parts of it. Whether these are ages in years or stages in the life of faith the text does not say.

decisions.choice: have been forgiven: forgiven once, and forgiven still
decisions.reason: The perfect ἀφέωνται describes forgiveness given in the past whose result lasts. The passive leaves God as the one who forgives (1:9).

decisions.choice: for the sake of his name: because of who Jesus is and what he has done
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person (John 1:12; 1 John 3:23; 5:13). "His" is Jesus, whose sacrifice (2:2) is the ground of forgiveness.

decisions.choice: stand forgiven
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the lasting result of the perfect (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: God has forgiven your sins for the sake of Jesus
alternatives: your sins have been forgiven because of his name
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who forgives (meaning decision m3) and Jesus as the one whose name is meant (m4), and makes the passive active.

decisions.choice: Dear children, I am writing to you
alternatives: I am writing to you, dear children
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the address first in each of the six sayings, as English letters do, so the three groups stand out. "Dear children" as in 2:1.

source.text: γράφω ὑμῖν, πατέρες, ὅτι ἐγνώκατε τὸν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς· γράφω ὑμῖν, νεανίσκοι, ὅτι νενικήκατε τὸν πονηρόν.

records.literal_gloss: I am writing to you, fathers, because you have known the [one] from [the] beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil [one].

en.L: I am writing to you, fathers, because you have come to know the [one who is] from [the] beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil [one].
en.B: Fathers, I am writing to you because you know the one who has been from the beginning. Young men, I am writing to you because you have defeated the evil one.
en.R: Fathers, I am writing to you because you know the one who was there from the very beginning. Young men, I am writing to you because you have won the fight against the evil one, the devil.

fr.L: Je vous écris, pères, parce que vous avez connu celui [qui est] depuis le commencement. Je vous écris, jeunes hommes, parce que vous avez vaincu le Mauvais.
fr.B: Pères, je vous écris parce que vous connaissez celui qui est depuis le commencement. Jeunes hommes, je vous écris parce que vous avez vaincu le Mauvais.
fr.R: Pères, je vous écris parce que vous connaissez celui qui existait déjà au tout début. Jeunes hommes, je vous écris parce que vous avez gagné le combat contre le Mauvais, le diable.

es.B: Padres, {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo porque {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} al que existe desde el principio. Jóvenes, {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo porque {{plural_you:han|habéis}} vencido al maligno.
es.R: Padres, {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo porque {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} al que estaba allí desde el mismo principio. Jóvenes, {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo porque {{plural_you:han|habéis}} ganado la lucha contra el maligno, el diablo.

sw.L: Ninawaandikia, akina baba, kwa kuwa mmekuja kumjua yule [aliyekuwapo] tangu mwanzo. Ninawaandikia, vijana, kwa kuwa mmekwisha kumshinda yule mwovu.
sw.B: Akina baba, nawaandikia kwa sababu mnamjua yule aliyekuwapo tangu mwanzo. Vijana, nawaandikia kwa sababu mmemshinda yule mwovu.
sw.R: Akina baba, nawaandikia kwa sababu mnamjua yule aliyekuwapo tangu mwanzo kabisa. Vijana, nawaandikia kwa sababu mmeshinda vita dhidi ya yule mwovu, yaani Ibilisi.

decisions.choice: fathers and young men: male words, kept as written; they may stand for the older and younger members of the whole church
alternatives: older and younger people, women included
only the men of the church
decisions.reason: πατέρες means fathers and νεανίσκοι young men; both are male words, and the text does not say whether women are meant. Letters of the time addressed parts of a community by their male members, and older and younger men were recognized groups (1 Timothy 5:1-2 and Titus 2:2-6 name older and younger women separately). Because the children of 2:12 are most likely the whole church (2:12, meaning decision m2), many read fathers and young men as two stages of faith that include women. That is a reading of the passage, not something the words themselves say, so the translation keeps the male words and a footnote gives the reading.

decisions.choice: the one who is from the beginning: Christ, who was with God before all things
decisions.reason: The letter opens with "what was from the beginning" (1:1), meaning the Word of life who became visible in Jesus (1:2; John 1:1-2). God is also eternal, and 2:14 adds "you know the Father" for the children, so the line could point to him. The parallel with 1:1 favors Christ.

decisions.choice: the evil one: the devil
decisions.reason: The masculine πονηρόν is a person: the devil (3:8, 3:10, 3:12; 5:18-19; John 17:15).

decisions.choice: you have known, you have overcome: what is already settled and still true
decisions.reason: Both verbs are perfect. The victory over the evil one is already won (4:4; 5:4-5; John 16:33), and the knowing began and continues.

decisions.choice: fathers; young men (no gender span)
decisions.reason: The gender setting is used where the original means men and women and only the wording differs. Here the Greek words are specifically male, and whether women are meant is a question of meaning (meaning decision m1), not of wording, so a setting cannot decide it. The footnote carries the inclusive reading.

decisions.choice: the evil one, the devil
decisions.reason: Readable names the evil one (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: have won the fight against
decisions.reason: Plainer words for young readers; Balanced says "defeated".

decisions.choice: jeunes hommes, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Greek words are male (m1), and the English keeps them without the gender setting. French "jeunes gens" is often read today as young people of both sexes, which would settle the question of meaning in the wording; "jeunes hommes" keeps it open as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: le Mauvais (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: "Le Malin" is the traditional name, but "malin" today mostly means clever or cunning. "Le Mauvais" says plainly that the evil one is meant (m3), and Readable adds "le diable", as the English does.

decisions.choice: padres; jóvenes, no gender span
decisions.reason: As in English, the male words are kept as written (meaning decision m1). Spanish "jóvenes" does not itself mark men only, which leaves open, as the note does, that the two groups may stand for older and younger members.

decisions.choice: akina baba; vijana
decisions.reason: The Greek words are male and are kept as written; they may stand for the older and younger members of the whole church (m1). "Akina baba" is the usual plural for fathers addressed as a group (as Ephesians 6:4); "vijana" (young men, youths) is the ordinary word and does not narrow the group further than the Greek.

decisions.choice: yule mwovu; yaani Ibilisi (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1 John 5:18-19: "yule mwovu" keeps John's title for a person (m3). Readable adds "yaani Ibilisi" (that is, the devil), as the English Readable adds "the devil".

source.text: ἔγραψα ὑμῖν, παιδία, ὅτι ἐγνώκατε τὸν πατέρα· ἔγραψα ὑμῖν, πατέρες, ὅτι ἐγνώκατε τὸν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς· ἔγραψα ὑμῖν, νεανίσκοι, ὅτι ἰσχυροί ἐστε καὶ ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν μένει καὶ νενικήκατε τὸν πονηρόν.

en.R: Children, I have written to you because you know the Father. Fathers, I have written to you because you know the one who was there from the very beginning. Young men, I have written to you because you are strong. God's word remains in you, and you have won the fight against the evil one, the devil.

Jeunes hommes, je vous ai écrit parce que vous êtes forts. La parole de Dieu demeure en vous, et vous avez gagné le combat contre le Mauvais, le diable.

Padres, {{plural_you:les|os}} he escrito porque {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} al que existe desde el principio. es.R: Hijos, {{plural_you:les|os}} he escrito porque {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} al Padre. Padres, {{plural_you:les|os}} he escrito porque {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} al que estaba allí desde el mismo principio. La palabra de Dios permanece en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y {{plural_you:han|habéis}} ganado la lucha contra el maligno, el diablo.

sw.L: Niliwaandikia, watoto, kwa kuwa mmekuja kumjua Baba. Niliwaandikia, akina baba, kwa kuwa mmekuja kumjua yule [aliyekuwapo] tangu mwanzo. Niliwaandikia, vijana, kwa kuwa mna nguvu, na neno la Mungu linakaa ndani yenu, nanyi mmekwisha kumshinda yule mwovu.
