sw.R: Watoto, nimewaandikia kwa sababu mnamjua Baba. Akina baba, nimewaandikia kwa sababu mnamjua yule aliyekuwapo tangu mwanzo kabisa. Vijana, nimewaandikia kwa sababu mna nguvu. Neno la Mungu linakaa ndani yenu, nanyi mmeshinda vita dhidi ya yule mwovu, yaani Ibilisi.

decisions.choice: I wrote: John looks at this same letter from a second angle; the change of tense is a matter of style
alternatives: an earlier letter, or John's Gospel
the part of this letter already written
a contrast between what he writes now and what he wrote before
decisions.reason: Three times John says "I am writing" (2:12-13), then three times ἔγραψα, with almost the same reasons. Greek letter writers could use the past tense for the letter in hand, seen from the time it would be read. The letter uses the same form for itself in 2:21, 2:26 and 5:13, and in 2:26 it clearly means this letter. No earlier letter is known. The repetition with a change of tense seems meant to press the same assurance home.

decisions.choice: children: a second warm word for all the readers
decisions.reason: παιδία stands where τεκνίον stood in 2:12, and is used again for the whole church in 2:18. The meaning is the same (2:12, meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: fathers, young men, the one from the beginning: as in 2:13
decisions.reason: See the notes on 2:13: the male words are kept (2:13, meaning decision m1), and "the one from the beginning" is most likely Christ.

decisions.choice: the word of God remains in you: God's message has taken root in you and stays
decisions.reason: The young men's strength lies in God's word living in them. Jesus speaks of his words remaining in his disciples (John 15:7) and of those in whom God's word does not remain (John 5:38).

decisions.choice: I wrote (L); I have written (B, R)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the change of tense visible, since its meaning is uncertain (meaning decision m1). "I have written" is how an English letter writer refers to his own letter.

decisions.choice: the evil one, the devil
decisions.reason: As in 2:13. No gender span on fathers or young men, as in 2:13.

decisions.choice: je vous ai écrit at every level, Literal included
decisions.reason: The English Literal says "I wrote" and Balanced "I have written". French has one natural form for a writer speaking of his own letter, the passé composé, and it still shows the change from "je vous écris" in 2:12-13 (m1); a passé simple would be out of place in a letter.

decisions.choice: hijos (for paidia)
decisions.reason: A second warm word for all the readers (meaning decision m2). "Hijos" keeps it apart from "hijitos" (teknia) while staying warm; "niños" would sound as if John meant young children. The same in 2:18.

decisions.choice: watoto (every level)
decisions.reason: A second warm word for all the readers (m2), different from the word in 2:1 and 2:12. Plain "watoto" (children) keeps the two apart, as the English keeps "children" and "dear children" apart.

source.text: Μὴ ἀγαπᾶτε τὸν κόσμον μηδὲ τὰ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Not love the world nor the things in the world.

en.L: Do not love the world, nor the things in the world.
en.B: Do not give your love to the world or to the things that are in it.
en.R: Do not love this world or the things that belong to it.

fr.L: N’aimez pas le monde, ni les choses qui sont dans le monde.
fr.B: Ne donnez pas votre amour au monde, ni à ce qui est dans le monde.
fr.R: N’aimez pas ce monde, ni les choses qui lui appartiennent.

es.L: No {{plural_you:amen|améis}} al mundo ni las cosas que hay en el mundo.
es.B: No {{plural_you:entreguen su|entreguéis vuestro}} amor al mundo ni a las cosas que hay en él.
es.R: No {{plural_you:amen|améis}} este mundo ni las cosas que le pertenecen.

sw.L: Msiupende ulimwengu, wala vitu vilivyomo ulimwenguni.
sw.B: Msiupende ulimwengu wala vitu vilivyomo ndani yake.
sw.R: Msiupende ulimwengu huu wala vitu vilivyo vyake.

decisions.choice: the world: human life organized apart from God and set against him
decisions.reason: In 2:2 the world is the people Christ died for. Here it is the world as a system that does not come from the Father (2:16) and is passing away (2:17), the world that hated Jesus and his disciples (John 15:18-19; 17:14-16). God loves the world of people (John 3:16); believers are not to love the world in this sense.

decisions.choice: do not love: a standing command
decisions.reason: A present imperative with Μὴ forbids something as a way of life. It does not by itself imply that they were already doing it.

decisions.choice: give your love to
decisions.reason: Balanced says what kind of love is meant: setting one's heart on something. Literal and Readable say "love".

decisions.choice: ulimwengu
decisions.reason: As in John's Gospel and 1 John 5:4: "ulimwengu" is the world as John uses it, human life organized apart from God (m1). "Dunia" is more often the earth itself.

source.text: ἐάν τις ἀγαπᾷ τὸν κόσμον, οὐκ ἔστιν ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ πατρὸς ἐν αὐτῷ·

records.literal_gloss: If anyone loves the world, not is the love of the Father in him;

en.L: If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: Whoever loves the world has no love for the Father in {{gender:them|him}}.
en.R: Anyone who loves the world does not love the Father.

fr.L: Si quelqu’un aime le monde, l’amour du Père n’est pas en lui.
fr.B: Celui qui aime le monde n’a pas en lui l’amour pour le Père.
fr.R: Celui qui aime le monde n’aime pas le Père.

es.L: Si alguno ama al mundo, el amor del Padre no está en {{gender:esa persona|él}}.
es.B: Quien ama al mundo no tiene en su corazón amor por el Padre.
es.R: Quien ama al mundo no ama al Padre.

sw.L: Mtu yeyote akiupenda ulimwengu, upendo wa Baba haumo ndani yake.
sw.B: Yeyote anayeupenda ulimwengu hana upendo kwa Baba ndani yake.
sw.R: Mtu anayeupenda ulimwengu hampendi Baba.

decisions.choice: the love of the Father: love for the Father
alternatives: the Father's love for that person
the kind of love that comes from the Father
decisions.reason: As in 2:5, the Greek can mean love for the Father or the Father's love. Here the contrast is between two loves in the one person, love for the world and love for the Father, so love for the Father is the more likely sense. It cannot be ruled out that John means the Father's love has no home in such a person.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: Anyone, man or woman, is meant. Readable needs no pronoun.

source.text: ὅτι πᾶν τὸ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῆς σαρκὸς καὶ ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν καὶ ἡ ἀλαζονεία τοῦ βίου, οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ πατρός, ἀλλὰ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου ἐστίν·

records.literal_gloss: Because all the [thing] in the world, the desire of the flesh and the desire of the eyes and the pride of the life, not is from the Father, but from the world is;

en.L: Because everything in the world, the desire of the flesh and the desire of the eyes and the arrogance of life, is not from the Father, but is from the world.
en.B: For everything in the world—the cravings of human nature, the greed of the eyes, and arrogant pride in what one has—does not come from the Father but comes from the world.
en.R: For nothing that belongs to the world comes from the Father. It all comes from the world: the selfish cravings of our human nature, the greedy wanting of our eyes, and the bragging about what we have.

fr.L: Car tout ce qui est dans le monde, le désir de la chair et le désir des yeux et l’arrogance de la vie, n’est pas du Père, mais est du monde.
fr.B: Car tout ce qui est dans le monde — les désirs de la chair, l’avidité des regards et l’orgueil que l’on tire de ce qu’on possède — ne vient pas du Père, mais vient du monde.
fr.R: Car rien de ce qui appartient au monde ne vient du Père. Tout cela vient du monde : les désirs égoïstes de notre nature humaine, l’envie d’avoir tout ce que nous voyons, et la vantardise à propos de ce que nous possédons.

es.L: Porque todo lo que hay en el mundo, el deseo de la carne y el deseo de los ojos y la arrogancia de la vida, no proviene del Padre, sino que proviene del mundo.
es.B: Porque todo lo que hay en el mundo —los deseos de la naturaleza humana, la codicia de los ojos y el orgullo arrogante por lo que uno tiene— no viene del Padre, sino del mundo.
es.R: Porque nada de lo que pertenece al mundo viene del Padre. Todo viene del mundo: los deseos egoístas de nuestra naturaleza humana, la codicia de lo que vemos con los ojos, y el presumir de lo que tenemos.

sw.L: Kwa sababu kila kilichomo ulimwenguni, tamaa ya mwili, na tamaa ya macho, na majivuno ya maisha, hakitoki kwa Baba, bali kinatoka kwa ulimwengu.
sw.B: Kwa maana kila kitu kilichomo ulimwenguni—tamaa za asili ya kibinadamu, uchu wa macho, na kiburi juu ya mali alizo nazo mtu—hakitokani na Baba, bali kinatokana na ulimwengu.
sw.R: Kwa maana hakuna kitu chochote cha ulimwengu kinachotoka kwa Baba. Vyote vinatoka kwa ulimwengu: tamaa za ubinafsi za asili yetu ya kibinadamu, kutamani kwa uchu kila tunachokiona, na kujivuna kwa ajili ya vitu tulivyo navyo.

decisions.choice: for: the reason for the commands of 2:15
decisions.reason: ὅτι explains why love for the world and love for the Father cannot go together: what the world consists of does not come from the Father.

decisions.choice: the desire of the flesh: the cravings of human nature turned in on itself
decisions.reason: σάρξ here is human nature apart from God (compare John 1:13; 3:6). The cravings include bodily ones but are not limited to them: whatever a person wants for self, apart from God.

decisions.choice: the desire of the eyes: wanting whatever one sees
decisions.reason: Seeing leads to craving: the woman saw that the tree was a delight to the eyes (Genesis 3:6), and Achan saw, desired and took (Joshua 7:21).

decisions.choice: the pride of life: arrogance about one's possessions and position
alternatives: boasting about one's way of life in general
decisions.reason: ἀλαζονεία is boastful pretension, the swagger of someone who makes much of what he has (James 4:16 uses a related word). βίος is not life as such but the means of life, one's livelihood and goods, as in 3:17, "the world's goods".

decisions.choice: three examples of what the world consists of
decisions.reason: The three phrases stand alongside "everything in the world" and describe it; they are not a full list of sins.

decisions.choice: cravings of human nature; greed of the eyes; arrogant pride in what one has
alternatives: the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life
decisions.reason: The traditional wording is well known but now misleading: "lust" suggests sexual desire, "flesh" the body, and "pride of life" says little (meaning decisions m2-m4). Literal keeps the Greek shape with "desire" and "flesh".

decisions.choice: For nothing that belongs to the world comes from the Father. It all comes from the world: ...
decisions.reason: Readable gives the main point first and the three examples after it, in two sentences.

decisions.choice: les désirs de la chair (B); l’avidité des regards; l’orgueil que l’on tire de ce qu’on possède
alternatives: les désirs de la nature humaine (B)
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "la chair" at Literal and Balanced, where the English Balanced says "human nature"; Readable follows the English and the meaning decision (m2). "Convoitise" is avoided, as the English avoids "lust": it now suggests sexual desire. "Ce qu’on possède" renders the word for one's life and means of living (m4).

decisions.choice: deseos de la naturaleza humana; codicia de los ojos; orgullo por lo que uno tiene
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps "carne", "ojos" and "vida"; Balanced and Readable say what each phrase means (meaning decisions m2-m4).

decisions.choice: majivuno ya maisha (L); kiburi juu ya mali alizo nazo mtu (B); kujivuna kwa ajili ya vitu tulivyo navyo (R)
decisions.reason: This word for life means one's livelihood, possessions and position (m4), not the life of God. So Swahili says "maisha", not "uzima", which is kept for the life of 1:1-2 and 2:25.

decisions.choice: tamaa ya mwili (L); tamaa za asili ya kibinadamu (B); tamaa za ubinafsi za asili yetu ya kibinadamu (R)
decisions.reason: The flesh here is human nature turned in on itself (m2), not the body only. Literal keeps "mwili"; Balanced and Readable say "human nature", as the English does, since "tamaa za kimwili" would suggest bodily appetites alone.

source.text: καὶ ὁ κόσμος παράγεται καὶ ἡ ἐπιθυμία αὐτοῦ, ὁ δὲ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.

records.literal_gloss: And the world is passing away and the desire of it, but the [one] doing the will of God remains into the age.

en.L: And the world is passing away, and its desire, but the one doing the will of God remains forever.
en.B: The world is passing away, and its cravings with it; but the one who does God's will remains forever.
en.R: The world is passing away, and so are all the things people crave in it. But anyone who does what God wants will remain forever.

fr.L: Et le monde passe, et son désir, mais celui qui fait la volonté de Dieu demeure pour l’éternité.
fr.B: Le monde passe, et ses désirs avec lui ; mais celui qui fait la volonté de Dieu demeure pour toujours.
fr.R: Le monde est en train de disparaître, et avec lui tout ce que les gens y désirent. Mais celui qui fait ce que Dieu veut demeurera pour toujours.

es.L: Y el mundo pasa, y su deseo, pero el que hace la voluntad de Dios permanece para siempre.
es.B: El mundo va pasando, y sus deseos con él; pero quien hace la voluntad de Dios permanece para siempre.
es.R: El mundo se está acabando, y también todo lo que la gente desea en él. Pero quien hace lo que Dios quiere permanecerá para siempre.

sw.L: Na ulimwengu unapita, na tamaa yake; lakini yule anayeyatenda mapenzi ya Mungu anakaa milele.
sw.B: Ulimwengu unapita, na tamaa zake pamoja nao; lakini anayetenda mapenzi ya Mungu anakaa milele.
sw.R: Ulimwengu unapita, pamoja na vitu vyote ambavyo watu huvitamani ndani yake. Lakini mtu anayefanya yale ambayo Mungu anataka atakaa milele.

decisions.choice: is passing away: already on its way out
decisions.reason: The same present tense was used of the darkness in 2:8. The world as it is now organized is already fading (1 Corinthians 7:31).

decisions.choice: its desire: the cravings the world stirs up, which pass with it
decisions.reason: αὐτοῦ refers back to the world. The cravings of 2:16 belong to the world and share its end.

decisions.choice: remains forever: lasts, sharing God's own life
decisions.reason: "Remains" is John's verb (2:6), set against "passing away". εἰς "into the age" is the ordinary Greek for "forever" (John 8:35). The one who does God's will shares the eternal life of 2:25.

decisions.choice: all the things people crave in it
decisions.reason: Readable spells out "its desire" (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: anakaa milele (L, B); atakaa milele (R)
decisions.reason: The same verb "remain" as elsewhere in the letter: the one who does God's will lasts, sharing God's own life (m3). "Kukaa" keeps it the same word; "kuishi milele" would say less than the Greek and lose the link.

source.text: Παιδία, ἐσχάτη ὥρα ἐστίν, καὶ καθὼς ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἀντίχριστος ἔρχεται, καὶ νῦν ἀντίχριστοι πολλοὶ γεγόνασιν· ὅθεν γινώσκομεν ὅτι ἐσχάτη ὥρα ἐστίν.

records.literal_gloss: Children, [the] last hour it is, and just as you heard that antichrist is coming, even now antichrists many have come about; from which we know that [the] last hour it is.

en.L: Children, it is [the] last hour; and just as you heard that antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have arisen. From this we know that it is [the] last hour.
en.B: Children, the last hour has come. You heard that the antichrist is coming, and in fact many antichrists have already appeared; that is how we know the last hour has come.
en.R: Children, we are living in the last hour. You heard that the antichrist, an enemy of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, is coming. Even now many antichrists have appeared. That is how we know that this is the last hour.

fr.L: Enfants, c’est la dernière heure, et comme vous avez entendu que l’antichrist vient, maintenant aussi beaucoup d’antichrists se sont levés ; par là nous savons que c’est la dernière heure.
fr.B: Enfants, la dernière heure est venue. Vous avez entendu dire que l’antichrist vient, et de fait beaucoup d’antichrists sont déjà apparus ; c’est ainsi que nous savons que la dernière heure est venue.
fr.R: Enfants, nous vivons la dernière heure. Vous avez entendu dire que l’antichrist, l’ennemi du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, va venir. Déjà maintenant, beaucoup d’antichrists sont apparus. C’est ainsi que nous savons que nous sommes dans la dernière heure.

es.L: Hijos, es [la] última hora; y así como {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} que viene el anticristo, también ahora han surgido muchos anticristos. Por esto sabemos que es [la] última hora.
es.B: Hijos, ha llegado la última hora. {{plural_you:Ustedes oyeron|Vosotros oísteis}} que viene el anticristo, y de hecho ya han aparecido muchos anticristos; por eso sabemos que ha llegado la última hora.
es.R: Hijos, estamos viviendo en la última hora. {{plural_you:Ustedes oyeron|Vosotros oísteis}} que viene el anticristo, un enemigo {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}. Ya ahora han aparecido muchos anticristos. Así es como sabemos que esta es la última hora.

sw.L: Watoto, ni saa ya mwisho; na kama mlivyosikia kwamba mpinga-Kristo anakuja, hata sasa wapinga-Kristo wengi wameshatokea. Kutokana na hili tunajua kwamba ni saa ya mwisho.
sw.B: Watoto, saa ya mwisho imefika. Mlisikia kwamba mpinga-Kristo anakuja, na kwa kweli wapinga-Kristo wengi wameshatokea; ndivyo tunavyojua kwamba saa ya mwisho imefika.
sw.R: Watoto, tunaishi katika saa ya mwisho. Mlisikia kwamba mpinga-Kristo, adui wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, anakuja. Hata sasa wapinga-Kristo wengi wametokea. Ndivyo tunavyojua kwamba hii ni saa ya mwisho.

decisions.choice: the last hour: the final period before Christ comes again, which has already begun
alternatives: the very last moment before the end
decisions.reason: The phrase is found only here in the New Testament. Jesus spoke of an hour that "is coming and now is" (John 5:25) and of raising his people "on the last day" (John 6:39-40). With Christ's coming, the last days had begun (Acts 2:17; Hebrews 1:2); John sees the appearance of many antichrists as a sign of it.

decisions.choice: antichrist: an opponent of Christ who sets himself up in Christ's place
decisions.reason: ἀντίχριστος joins a word meaning "against" or "instead of" to "Christ". The word appears only in John's letters (2:18, 2:22; 4:3; 2 John 7). The readers had been taught to expect one great opponent before the end (compare 2 Thessalonians 2:3-4; Mark 13:22). John says the spirit of that opponent is already at work in many people, those who deny that Jesus is the Christ (2:22).

decisions.choice: antichrist is coming: a figure the readers already knew of
decisions.reason: ἀντίχριστος has no article, but the readers had heard of this figure as someone particular, so it is treated almost as a name.

decisions.choice: have arisen: they have come on the scene and are present now
decisions.reason: The perfect γεγόνασιν describes something that has happened and whose result is present: the antichrists are already here.

decisions.choice: antichrist, antichrists (lowercase, no title setting)
decisions.reason: "Antichrist" is an English word taken from the Greek, so it keeps its form when the title setting changes "Christ" to "Messiah". It is lowercase because many people bear it. Readable explains it once.

decisions.choice: the antichrist, an enemy of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: the last hour has come
decisions.reason: Says that the time has arrived (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: l’antichrist, les antichrists, lowercase and with no title setting, as in 2 John
decisions.reason: French has the word from the Greek too, so it keeps its form when the setting changes "Christ" to "Messie". French needs an article with it, which Literal does not bracket; "un antichrist" would hide that the readers already knew of the figure (m3).

decisions.choice: anticristo, anticristos, no christos span
decisions.reason: As in 2 John 7: "anticristo" is one word, and the setting does not split it. Literal says "el anticristo" because Spanish needs the article here; the Greek has none.

decisions.choice: mpinga-Kristo, wapinga-Kristo, no christos span
decisions.reason: As in 2 John 7: "mpinga-Kristo" names the expected opponent of Christ (m2), and the setting does not split the name. Readable explains it as "adui wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}" (enemy of Christ), where the setting applies, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: saa ya mwisho
decisions.reason: The final period before Christ comes again (m1). "Saa" means both hour and time in Swahili, so "saa ya mwisho" keeps John's word without suggesting a clock hour.

source.text: ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξῆλθαν, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἦσαν ἐξ ἡμῶν· εἰ γὰρ ἐξ ἡμῶν ἦσαν, μεμενήκεισαν ἂν μεθ’ ἡμῶν· ἀλλ’ ἵνα φανερωθῶσιν ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶν πάντες ἐξ ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: From us they went out, but not they were of us; for if of us they had been, they would have remained with us; but [it was] so that they might be revealed that not are all of us.

en.L: They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would have remained with us. But [they went out] so that it might be made plain that none of them are of us.
en.B: They went out from among us, but they were never truly part of us. If they had been part of us, they would have remained with us. Their leaving happened so that it would be made plain that none of them are part of us.
en.R: These people left our group, but they never really belonged to us. If they had belonged to us, they would have remained with us. But they left, and that made it clear that none of them really belonged to us.

fr.L: Ils sont sortis du milieu de nous, mais ils n’étaient pas des nôtres ; car s’ils avaient été des nôtres, ils seraient demeurés avec nous. Mais [ils sont sortis] afin qu’il soit rendu manifeste qu’aucun d’eux n’est des nôtres.
fr.B: Ils sont sortis de nos rangs, mais ils n’ont jamais vraiment été des nôtres. S’ils avaient été des nôtres, ils seraient restés avec nous. Leur départ a eu lieu pour qu’il apparaisse clairement qu’aucun d’eux n’est des nôtres.
fr.R: Ces gens ont quitté notre groupe, mais ils n’ont jamais vraiment été des nôtres. S’ils avaient été des nôtres, ils seraient restés avec nous. Mais ils sont partis, et cela a montré clairement qu’aucun d’eux n’était vraiment des nôtres.

es.L: De nosotros salieron, pero no eran de nosotros; porque si hubieran sido de nosotros, habrían permanecido con nosotros. Pero [salieron] para que se hiciera manifiesto que no todos son de nosotros.
es.B: Salieron de entre nosotros, pero nunca fueron realmente de los nuestros. Si hubieran sido de los nuestros, habrían permanecido con nosotros. Su salida sucedió para que quedara claro que ninguno de ellos es de los nuestros.
es.R: Esas personas dejaron nuestro grupo, pero nunca nos pertenecieron de verdad. Si hubieran sido de los nuestros, se habrían quedado con nosotros. Pero se fueron, y eso dejó claro que ninguno de ellos era de verdad de los nuestros.

sw.L: Walitoka kati yetu, lakini hawakuwa wa kwetu; kwa kuwa kama wangekuwa wa kwetu, wangekaa pamoja nasi; lakini [walitoka] ili idhihirike kwamba hakuna hata mmoja wao aliye wa kwetu.
sw.B: Walitoka miongoni mwetu, lakini kwa kweli hawakuwa sehemu yetu. Kama wangekuwa sehemu yetu, wangekaa pamoja nasi. Kuondoka kwao kulitokea ili ionekane wazi kwamba hakuna hata mmoja wao aliye sehemu yetu.
sw.R: Watu hawa waliondoka katika kikundi chetu, lakini hawakuwa kamwe wenzetu kwa kweli. Kama wangekuwa wenzetu, wangekaa pamoja nasi. Lakini waliondoka, na jambo hilo lilionyesha wazi kwamba hakuna hata mmoja wao aliye mwenzetu kwa kweli.

decisions.choice: they went out: the antichrists of 2:18 were people who had left the community
decisions.reason: A group had broken away from the churches John writes to. The letter does not tell their story, but it shows they denied that Jesus is the Christ (2:22) and were still trying to win others over (2:26; 4:1-5; 2 John 7).

decisions.choice: of us: belonging to us, sharing our life
decisions.reason: The same words are used two ways: "from us" (they left our company) and "of us" (they belonged to us). They had been in the church without truly belonging to it.

decisions.choice: but this happened so that: their leaving served a purpose
decisions.reason: The clause has no main verb; "they went out" or "this happened" is understood. Their departure brought into the open what had been hidden.

decisions.choice: none of them are of us
alternatives: not all who are among us are truly of us
decisions.reason: οὐκ with πάντες can mean "not all" or, as often in Greek shaped by Hebrew, "none". Read as "none", John says all who left showed they never belonged. Read as "not all", he says that not everyone in a church truly belongs to it. The subject "they" of the clause before favors "none of them".

decisions.choice: would have remained: would have stayed in fellowship with us
decisions.reason: John's verb "remain" (2:6). Staying with the community goes with remaining in God (1:3).

decisions.choice: [they went out] (L); Their leaving happened (B)
decisions.reason: The understood main verb is supplied (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: qu’aucun d’eux n’est des nôtres
alternatives: que tous ne sont pas des nôtres
decisions.reason: French "tous ne sont pas" would be read as "not all of them", which is not how the sentence is taken here (m4); "aucun d’eux" says "none of them", as the English does.

decisions.choice: no todos son de nosotros (L); ninguno de ellos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek words, which in Spanish can also be heard as "not all"; meaning decision m4 reads them as "none of them", which Balanced and Readable say.

decisions.choice: se habrían quedado (R)
decisions.reason: Here the verb means staying with the community, not the abiding of verse 6, so Readable uses the everyday "quedarse"; Literal and Balanced keep "permanecer".

decisions.choice: hakuna hata mmoja wao
decisions.reason: The Greek "not all" here means "none" (m4). "Si wote" (not all) would say that some of them do belong, so every level says "hakuna hata mmoja wao" (not one of them).

source.text: καὶ ὑμεῖς χρῖσμα ἔχετε ἀπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου καὶ οἴδατε πάντες·

records.literal_gloss: And you an anointing have from the Holy [One] and you know all.

en.L: And you have an anointing from the Holy [One], and you all know.
en.B: But as for you, the Holy One has anointed you, and you all know the truth.
en.R: But you are not like them. The Holy One has anointed you, and all of you know the truth.

fr.L: Et vous, vous avez une onction de la part du Saint, et vous savez tous.
fr.B: Mais vous, le Saint vous a oints, et vous connaissez tous la vérité.
fr.R: Mais vous, vous n’êtes pas comme eux. Le Saint vous a oints, et vous connaissez tous la vérité.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:ustedes tienen|vosotros tenéis}} una unción del Santo, y todos {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}}.
es.B: Pero en cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, el Santo {{plural_you:los|os}} ha ungido, y todos {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} la verdad.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes no son|vosotros no sois}} como ellos. El Santo {{plural_you:los|os}} ha ungido, y todos {{plural_you:ustedes conocen|vosotros conocéis}} la verdad.

sw.L: Nanyi mna upako kutoka kwa yule Mtakatifu, nanyi nyote mnajua.
sw.B: Lakini ninyi, yule Mtakatifu amewapaka mafuta, nanyi nyote mnaijua kweli.
sw.R: Lakini ninyi si kama wao. Yule Mtakatifu amewapaka mafuta, na ninyi nyote mnaijua kweli.

decisions.choice: and you: in contrast to those who left
decisions.reason: The pronoun ὑμεῖς is emphatic, and καὶ marks a contrast here: unlike the antichrists, you have the anointing.

decisions.choice: anointing: what God has poured on believers, most likely the Holy Spirit
alternatives: God's word, the message they heard (2:24)
an anointing with oil at baptism
decisions.reason: χρῖσμα is what one is anointed with. In 2:27 it teaches them and remains in them, which Jesus says of the Spirit (John 14:16-17, 14:26; 16:13), and Jesus himself was anointed with the Spirit (Acts 10:38). Others note that 2:24 says it is what they heard from the beginning that must remain in them, and take the anointing as God's word received by faith. The two are close: the Spirit teaches through the message.

decisions.choice: anointing and Christ: the same root
decisions.reason: χρῖσμα comes from the same root as Χριστός, the Anointed One. The antichrists deny that Jesus is the Christ (2:22); believers share in his anointing.

decisions.choice: the Holy One: Christ, or God
decisions.reason: Peter calls Jesus "the Holy One of God" (John 6:69), and 2:27 says the anointing comes "from him", meaning Christ (2:28). God is also called holy throughout Scripture. The text does not decide.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "you all know"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has πάντες, a masculine plural: "all of you know". Many manuscripts have instead the neuter plural, "you know all things". From general knowledge, the first reading is found in some important early manuscripts (including Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus) and the second in others (including Codex Alexandrinus) and in most later ones. A copyist may have changed the text to give "know" an object, or to match "teaches you about all things" in 2:27. With the SBLGNT reading the point is that every believer knows the truth, not only a few with special knowledge. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Holy One has anointed you
alternatives: you have an anointing from the Holy One
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the noun into a verb, which reads more naturally and keeps the link with "Christ", the Anointed One (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps the noun, as 2:27 does at every level.

decisions.choice: know the truth
decisions.reason: The Greek "know" has no object; 2:21 supplies it: "you know the truth". Literal leaves it out.

decisions.choice: But you are not like them.
decisions.reason: Readable makes the contrast with those who left explicit (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: une onction (L); vous a oints (B, R); l’onction at every level in 2:27
decisions.reason: As in English, Balanced and Readable turn the noun into the verb "oindre", which keeps the link with "Christ", the "Oint" (m3). The meaning that the anointing is most likely the Spirit (m2) is left to the notes, as the English leaves it.

decisions.choice: unción (L); ungir (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Unción" and "ungir" share their root with "Ungido", as the Greek word shares its root with "Christ" (meaning decision m3); Spanish keeps the link as far as it can.

decisions.choice: upako (L); amewapaka mafuta (B, R)
decisions.reason: The anointing is what God has poured on believers, most likely the Holy Spirit (m2). Literal keeps the noun "upako"; Balanced and Readable use the verb "kupaka mafuta", as the English says "has anointed you". The Greek ties this word to "Christ" (Anointed One, m3); Swahili "Kristo" is a borrowed name and cannot show the link.

source.text: οὐκ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν ἀλήθειαν, ἀλλ’ ὅτι οἴδατε αὐτήν, καὶ ὅτι πᾶν ψεῦδος ἐκ τῆς ἀληθείας οὐκ ἔστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Not I wrote to you because not you know the truth, but because you know it, and because every lie from the truth not is.

en.L: I did not write to you because you do not know the truth, but because you know it, and because no lie is from the truth.
en.B: My reason for writing to you is not that you are ignorant of the truth. It is that you know it, and that nothing false ever comes from the truth.
en.R: I have not written to you because you do not know the truth. I have written because you do know it, and because no lie can come from the truth.

fr.L: Je ne vous ai pas écrit parce que vous ne connaissez pas la vérité, mais parce que vous la connaissez, et parce qu’aucun mensonge n’est de la vérité.
fr.B: Si je vous écris, ce n’est pas que vous ignoriez la vérité. C’est que vous la connaissez, et que rien de faux ne vient jamais de la vérité.
fr.R: Je ne vous ai pas écrit parce que vous ne connaissez pas la vérité. Je vous ai écrit parce que vous la connaissez bien, et parce qu’aucun mensonge ne peut venir de la vérité.

es.L: No {{plural_you:les|os}} escribí porque no {{plural_you:conozcan|conozcáis}} la verdad, sino porque la {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}}, y porque ninguna mentira procede de la verdad.
es.B: No {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo porque {{plural_you:ignoren|ignoréis}} la verdad, sino porque la {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}}, y porque nada falso procede jamás de la verdad.
es.R: No {{plural_you:les|os}} he escrito porque no {{plural_you:conozcan|conozcáis}} la verdad. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he escrito porque sí la {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}}, y porque ninguna mentira puede venir de la verdad.

sw.L: Sikuwaandikia kwa kuwa hamuijui kweli, bali kwa kuwa mnaijua, na kwa kuwa uongo wowote hautoki katika kweli.
sw.B: Sababu ya kuwaandikia si kwamba hamuijui kweli. Ni kwamba mnaijua, na kwamba hakuna uongo wowote unaotokana na kweli.
sw.R: Sijawaandikia kwa sababu hamuijui kweli. Nimewaandikia kwa sababu mnaijua, na kwa sababu hakuna uongo unaoweza kutoka katika kweli.

decisions.choice: I wrote: this letter
decisions.reason: As in 2:14, the past tense refers to what John is writing now.

decisions.choice: because ... because ... because: three reasons for writing
alternatives: the third clause says what they know: "you know it, and you know that no lie comes from the truth"
decisions.reason: The first two uses of ὅτι clearly give reasons. The third could add a further reason or say a second thing they know. Read as a reason, it keeps the three clauses parallel.

decisions.choice: every lie ... is not: no lie at all
decisions.reason: πᾶν with a negative is a Hebrew way of saying "none".

decisions.choice: lie: falsehood about God and his Son, above all the denial of 2:22
decisions.reason: The lie John has in mind is named in the next verse: denying that Jesus is the Christ.

decisions.choice: My reason for writing to you is not that ... It is that ...
alternatives: I have not written to you because ... but because ...
decisions.reason: Balanced restates the negative and positive reasons as two plain sentences.

source.text: τίς ἐστιν ὁ ψεύστης εἰ μὴ ὁ ἀρνούμενος ὅτι Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ χριστός;

records.literal_gloss: Who is the liar if not the [one] denying that Jesus not is the Christ?

en.L: Who is the liar except the one denying that Jesus is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?
en.B: Who is the liar, if not the person who denies that Jesus is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?
en.R: Who is the real liar? It is anyone who says that Jesus is not the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

fr.L: Qui est le menteur, sinon celui qui nie que Jésus soit le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} ?
fr.B: Qui est le menteur, si ce n’est celui qui nie que Jésus soit le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} ?
fr.R: Qui est le vrai menteur ? C’est celui qui dit que Jésus n’est pas le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

es.L: ¿Quién es el mentiroso, sino el que niega que Jesús es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?
es.B: ¿Quién es el mentiroso, sino la persona que niega que Jesús es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?
es.R: ¿Quién es el verdadero mentiroso? Es cualquiera que dice que Jesús no es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}.

sw.L: Mwongo ni nani, ila yule anayekana kwamba Yesu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?
sw.B: Ni nani aliye mwongo, kama si mtu anayekana kwamba Yesu ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?
sw.R: Mwongo halisi ni nani? Ni mtu yeyote anayesema kwamba Yesu si {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

decisions.choice: denies that Jesus is the Christ
alternatives: denies that Jesus is not the Christ
decisions.reason: After a verb of denying, Greek can add a negative that only repeats the denial; οὐκ is not translated.

decisions.choice: the liar: the liar above all others
decisions.reason: The article marks this as the lie of all lies, the one behind the others (2:21).

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Anointed One God promised, who is the Son of God
decisions.reason: To deny that Jesus is the Christ is, for this letter, to deny that the man Jesus is the Son who came from the Father (2:23; 4:2-3; 5:1, 5:5-6). The letter does not set out what the deniers taught; the stress on Jesus coming "in the flesh" (4:2) suggests they separated the human Jesus from the Christ.

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting; with the article, "the" stays outside the span at every level, as in John 1:20.

decisions.choice: Who is the real liar? It is anyone who says ...
decisions.reason: Readable answers the question in a second sentence; "real" brings out the article (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}
decisions.reason: As in 1 John 5:1: "Christ" is a title with the article, so the article stays outside the span.

decisions.choice: kukana
decisions.reason: To deny is to refuse to own the truth about Jesus (m1). "Kukana" is the word for denying a person or a truth, as in the Gospels. Readable says "anayesema kwamba Yesu si" (says that Jesus is not) here and "kukataa kumkubali" (refuse to accept) in 2:22b-23, as the English Readable does.

source.text: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἀντίχριστος, ὁ ἀρνούμενος τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὸν υἱόν.

records.literal_gloss: This is the antichrist, the [one] denying the Father and the Son.

en.L: This one is the antichrist, the one denying the Father and the Son.
en.B: That person is the antichrist, the one who denies the Father as well as the Son.
en.R: A person like that is the antichrist. {{gender:They refuse|He refuses}} to accept the Father and the Son.

fr.L: Celui-là est l’antichrist, celui qui renie le Père et le Fils.
fr.B: Celui-là, c’est l’antichrist : il renie le Père aussi bien que le Fils.
fr.R: Celui qui fait cela est l’antichrist. Il refuse d’accepter le Père et le Fils.

es.L: Este es el anticristo, el que niega al Padre y al Hijo.
es.B: Esa persona es el anticristo, el que niega al Padre y también al Hijo.
es.R: Una persona así es el anticristo. Se niega a aceptar al Padre y al Hijo.

sw.L: Huyu ndiye mpinga-Kristo: yule anayemkana Baba na kumkana Mwana.
sw.B: Mtu huyo ndiye mpinga-Kristo, anayemkana Baba pamoja na Mwana.
sw.R: Mtu wa namna hiyo ndiye mpinga-Kristo. Anakataa kumkubali Baba na Mwana.

decisions.choice: this one: the person who denies that Jesus is the Christ
decisions.reason: οὗτός points back to the denier in the question just asked.

decisions.choice: denying the Son is denying the Father
alternatives: denying the Father and denying the Son as two separate errors
decisions.reason: One article stands with each name, but the participle is single: one act of denial rejects both, because the Father is known only through the Son (2:23; John 5:23; 14:9).

decisions.choice: {{gender:They refuse|He refuses}}
decisions.reason: Anyone, man or woman, who denies is meant. Literal and Balanced need no pronoun.

decisions.choice: refuse to accept
decisions.reason: A plainer phrase for disowning someone.

source.text: πᾶς ὁ ἀρνούμενος τὸν υἱὸν οὐδὲ τὸν πατέρα ἔχει· ὁ ὁμολογῶν τὸν υἱὸν καὶ τὸν πατέρα ἔχει.

records.literal_gloss: Everyone denying the Son neither the Father has; the [one] confessing the Son also the Father has.

en.L: Everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father either; the one who confesses the Son has the Father also.
en.B: Anyone who denies the Son is without the Father as well; anyone who confesses the Son has the Father too.
en.R: Anyone who refuses to accept the Son does not have the Father either. But anyone who openly acknowledges the Son has the Father too.

fr.L: Quiconque renie le Fils n’a pas non plus le Père ; celui qui confesse le Fils a aussi le Père.
fr.B: Quiconque renie le Fils est sans le Père lui aussi ; celui qui confesse le Fils a aussi le Père.
fr.R: Celui qui refuse d’accepter le Fils n’a pas non plus le Père. Mais celui qui reconnaît ouvertement le Fils a aussi le Père.

es.L: Todo el que niega al Hijo tampoco tiene al Padre; el que confiesa al Hijo tiene también al Padre.
es.B: Quien niega al Hijo está también sin el Padre; quien confiesa al Hijo tiene también al Padre.
es.R: Quien se niega a aceptar al Hijo tampoco tiene al Padre. Pero quien reconoce abiertamente al Hijo tiene también al Padre.

sw.L: Yeyote anayemkana Mwana, hata Baba hanaye; yule anayemkiri Mwana, Baba pia anaye.
sw.B: Yeyote anayemkana Mwana hana Baba vilevile; yeyote anayemkiri Mwana ana Baba pia.
sw.R: Yeyote anayekataa kumkubali Mwana hana Baba pia. Lakini yeyote anayemkiri Mwana waziwazi ana Baba pia.

decisions.choice: has the Father: belongs to him and shares his life
decisions.reason: To "have" God is to be in a living relationship with him (2 John 9). "Whoever has the Son has life" (5:12).

decisions.choice: confess: declare openly who the Son is
decisions.reason: ὁμολογέω is to say in public what one believes (4:2, 4:15; John 9:22). Here it is the opposite of denying the Son.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: the second half of the verse is part of the text
alternatives: omit "the one who confesses the Son has the Father also"
decisions.reason: From general knowledge, the early manuscripts have the second half of the verse, while many later ones leave it out; the King James Version printed it in italics. A copyist's eye could easily skip from the first "has" to the second, which end both halves. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: refuses to accept; openly acknowledges
decisions.reason: Plainer words for young readers. "Confess" now usually means admitting a fault.

decisions.choice: kumkiri Mwana
decisions.reason: To confess is to declare openly who the Son is (m2). "Kukiri" is the word for confessing a person or a truth, and is kept apart from "kuungama", which 1:9 uses for confessing sins. Readable adds "waziwazi" (openly), as the English Readable says "openly acknowledges".

source.text: ὑμεῖς ὃ ἠκούσατε ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς, ἐν ὑμῖν μενέτω· ἐὰν ἐν ὑμῖν μείνῃ ὃ ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ἠκούσατε, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐν τῷ υἱῷ καὶ ἐν τῷ πατρὶ μενεῖτε.

records.literal_gloss: You, what you heard from [the] beginning, in you let it remain. If in you remains what from [the] beginning you heard, also you in the Son and in the Father will remain.

en.L: As for you, what you heard from [the] beginning, let it remain in you. If what you heard from [the] beginning remains in you, you also will remain in the Son and in the Father.
en.B: You, for your part, must let what you heard from the beginning remain in you. If what you heard from the beginning remains in you, you too will remain in the Son and in the Father.
en.R: So let the message you heard at the very beginning remain in your hearts. If it remains in you, you will also remain in the Son and in the Father.

fr.L: Vous, ce que vous avez entendu depuis le commencement, que cela demeure en vous. Si ce que vous avez entendu depuis le commencement demeure en vous, vous aussi, vous demeurerez dans le Fils et dans le Père.
fr.B: Quant à vous, faites en sorte que ce que vous avez entendu depuis le commencement demeure en vous. Si ce que vous avez entendu depuis le commencement demeure en vous, vous aussi vous demeurerez dans le Fils et dans le Père.
fr.R: Alors, que le message que vous avez entendu au tout début demeure dans votre cœur. S’il demeure en vous, vous demeurerez vous aussi dans le Fils et dans le Père.

es.L: En cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, lo que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} desde [el] principio, que permanezca en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Si permanece en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} lo que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} desde [el] principio, también {{plural_you:ustedes permanecerán|vosotros permaneceréis}} en el Hijo y en el Padre.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, por {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} parte, {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} que permanezca en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} lo que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} desde el principio. Si lo que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} desde el principio permanece en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, también {{plural_you:ustedes permanecerán|vosotros permaneceréis}} en el Hijo y en el Padre.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} que el mensaje que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} desde el mismo principio permanezca en {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón. Si permanece en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, también {{plural_you:permanecerán|permaneceréis}} en el Hijo y en el Padre.

sw.L: Ninyi, kile mlichosikia tangu mwanzo, kiacheni kikae ndani yenu. Ikiwa kile mlichosikia tangu mwanzo kitakaa ndani yenu, ninyi pia mtakaa katika Mwana na katika Baba.
sw.B: Ninyi, kwa upande wenu, hakikisheni kwamba kile mlichosikia tangu mwanzo kinakaa ndani yenu. Kama kile mlichosikia tangu mwanzo kinakaa ndani yenu, nanyi pia mtakaa ndani ya Mwana na ndani ya Baba.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo, ujumbe mliousikia mwanzoni kabisa na ukae mioyoni mwenu. Ukikaa ndani yenu, mtakaa pia ndani ya Mwana na ndani ya Baba.

decisions.choice: you: emphatic, in contrast to the deceivers
decisions.reason: ὑμεῖς stands first, ahead of its clause: whatever others do, you must hold to what you heard.

decisions.choice: what you heard from the beginning: the message about Jesus they received when they first believed
decisions.reason: As in 2:7 and 3:11. Against teachers who offered something new, John points them back to the message they started with.

decisions.choice: remain in the Son and in the Father
decisions.reason: If the message remains in them, they remain in the Son and so in the Father (2:23). The order, Son first, follows the way to the Father (John 14:6).

decisions.choice: remain in your hearts
decisions.reason: Readable says where the message is to remain; "in you" alone is vague for young readers.

decisions.choice: If it remains in you
alternatives: If what you heard from the beginning remains in you
decisions.reason: Readable does not repeat the long phrase.

source.text: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἐπαγγελία ἣν αὐτὸς ἐπηγγείλατο ἡμῖν, τὴν ζωὴν τὴν αἰώνιον.

records.literal_gloss: And this is the promise which he promised us, the life the eternal.

en.L: And this is the promise that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} promised us: the eternal life.
en.B: And the promise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} made to us is this: eternal life.
en.R: And this is what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} has promised us: eternal life, the life of God's new age, which begins now.

fr.L: Et telle est la promesse qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} promise : la vie éternelle.
fr.B: Et la promesse qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a faite {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, la voici : la vie éternelle.
fr.R: Et voici ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a promis {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} : la vie éternelle, la vie du monde nouveau de Dieu, qui commence dès maintenant.

es.L: Y esta es la promesa que {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}} nos prometió: la vida eterna.
es.B: Y la promesa que {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}} nos hizo es esta: la vida eterna.
es.R: Y esto es lo que {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}} nos ha prometido: la vida eterna, la vida de la nueva era de Dios, que comienza ya ahora.

sw.L: Na ahadi aliyotuahidi {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ni hii: uzima wa milele.
sw.B: Ahadi ambayo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ametupa ni hii: uzima wa milele.
sw.R: Na hiki ndicho {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ametuahidi: uzima wa milele, yaani uzima wa ulimwengu mpya wa Mungu, unaoanza hata sasa.

decisions.choice: this is the promise: eternal life
alternatives: this (the promise) refers back to remaining in the Son and the Father
decisions.reason: αὕτη points forward to "eternal life", which stands at the end of the sentence. It is in the same case as the relative pronoun, a common Greek construction, but it explains the promise.

decisions.choice: he: Christ, or God
decisions.reason: Jesus gives eternal life (John 10:28; 17:2), and the Son was named last (2:24). The letter also says God gave us eternal life in his Son (5:11). αὐτὸς is emphatic: he himself made the promise.

decisions.choice: eternal life: the life of the age to come, God's own life, which believers have now
decisions.reason: The letter opened by announcing "the eternal life that was with the Father" (1:2). Believers have it already (5:11-13; John 5:24).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}
decisions.reason: Pronouns for God or Christ take the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: the life of God's new age, which begins now
decisions.reason: Readable explains eternal life once in the passage (meaning decision m3).

source.text: Ταῦτα ἔγραψα ὑμῖν περὶ τῶν πλανώντων ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: These things I wrote to you concerning the [ones] leading astray you.

en.L: These things I wrote to you about those who are leading you astray.
en.B: I have written these things to you concerning those who are out to deceive you.
en.R: I have written these things to warn you about the people who are trying to fool you.

fr.L: Je vous ai écrit ces choses au sujet de ceux qui vous égarent.
fr.B: Je vous ai écrit ces choses à propos de ceux qui cherchent à vous égarer.
fr.R: Je vous ai écrit ces choses pour vous mettre en garde contre les gens qui essaient de vous tromper.

es.L: Estas cosas {{plural_you:les|os}} escribí acerca de los que {{plural_you:los|os}} están extraviando.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he escrito estas cosas acerca de los que buscan {{plural_you:engañarlos|engañaros}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he escrito estas cosas para {{plural_you:advertirles|advertiros}} acerca de las personas que están tratando de {{plural_you:engañarlos|engañaros}}.

sw.L: Mambo haya niliwaandikia kuhusu wale wanaowapotosha.
sw.B: Nimewaandikia mambo haya kuhusu wale wanaotaka kuwapotosha.
sw.R: Nimewaandikia mambo haya ili kuwaonya juu ya watu wanaojaribu kuwadanganya.

decisions.choice: leading you astray: trying to, not yet succeeding
decisions.reason: The present participle πλανώντων describes an effort still going on. The readers have not been won over (2:20-21, 2:27).

decisions.choice: lead astray: deceive, draw off the right path
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in 1:8 and 3:7, and the deceivers are named in 2 John 7. They are the people of 2:19.

decisions.choice: I wrote: this letter, especially 2:18-25
decisions.reason: As in 2:14 and 2:21.

decisions.choice: to warn you about
decisions.reason: Readable says why he writes about them.

decisions.choice: wanaowapotosha (L); wanaotaka kuwapotosha (B); wanaojaribu kuwadanganya (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to draw off the right path (m2), and they are trying, not yet succeeding (m1). "Kupotosha" (lead astray) is the word used for the deceivers in 2 John 7; Readable says "kudanganya" (fool), as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ὑμεῖς τὸ χρῖσμα ὃ ἐλάβετε ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ μένει ἐν ὑμῖν, καὶ οὐ χρείαν ἔχετε ἵνα τις διδάσκῃ ὑμᾶς· ἀλλ’ ὡς τὸ αὐτοῦ χρῖσμα διδάσκει ὑμᾶς περὶ πάντων, καὶ ἀληθές ἐστιν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ψεῦδος, καὶ καθὼς ἐδίδαξεν ὑμᾶς, μένετε ἐν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And you, the anointing which you received from him remains in you, and not need you have that anyone should teach you; but as the of him anointing teaches you concerning all things, and true is and not is a lie, and just as it taught you, remain in him.

en.L: And as for you, the anointing that you received from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} remains in you, and you have no need that anyone should teach you. But as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointing teaches you about all things, and is true and is not a lie, and just as [the anointing] taught you, remain in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: As for you, you received an anointing from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and that anointing remains in you; you have no need for anyone to teach you. Rather, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointing teaches you about everything, and is true and not a lie. So, just as the anointing has taught you, remain in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: But you received an anointing from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and that anointing remains in you. So you do not need anyone to teach you. The anointing from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} teaches you about everything. That teaching is true, not a lie. So remain in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, just as you have been taught.

fr.L: Et vous, l’onction que vous avez reçue de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demeure en vous, et vous n’avez pas besoin que quelqu’un vous enseigne ; mais comme {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} onction vous enseigne au sujet de toutes choses, et elle est vraie et n’est pas mensonge, et selon qu’elle vous a enseignés, demeurez en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Quant à vous, vous avez reçu de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} l’onction, et cette onction demeure en vous ; vous n’avez besoin de personne pour vous enseigner. Au contraire, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} onction vous enseigne tout, et elle est vraie, elle n’est pas mensonge. Alors, comme elle vous l’a enseigné, demeurez en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Mais vous avez reçu de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} l’onction, et elle demeure en vous. Vous n’avez donc besoin de personne pour vous enseigner. L’onction qui vient de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} vous enseigne tout. Cet enseignement est vrai, ce n’est pas un mensonge. Alors demeurez en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, comme vous l’avez appris.

es.L: Y en cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, la unción que {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}} de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} permanece en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} necesidad de que nadie {{plural_you:les|os}} enseñe. Pero como {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} unción {{plural_you:les|os}} enseña acerca de todas las cosas, y es verdadera y no es mentira, y así como [la unción] {{plural_you:les|os}} enseñó, {{plural_you:permanezcan|permaneced}} en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: En cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}} de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} una unción, y esa unción permanece en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; no {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}} que nadie {{plural_you:les|os}} enseñe. Al contrario, {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} unción {{plural_you:les|os}} enseña acerca de todo, y es verdadera y no mentira. Así que, tal como la unción {{plural_you:les|os}} ha enseñado, {{plural_you:permanezcan|permaneced}} en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes recibieron|vosotros recibisteis}} de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} una unción, y esa unción permanece en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Por eso no {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}} que nadie {{plural_you:les|os}} enseñe. La unción que viene de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:les|os}} enseña acerca de todo. Esa enseñanza es verdadera, no es mentira. Así que {{plural_you:permanezcan|permaneced}} en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, tal como se {{plural_you:les|os}} ha enseñado.

sw.L: Nanyi, upako mlioupokea kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} unakaa ndani yenu, wala hamna haja mtu yeyote awafundishe; lakini kama upako {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} unavyowafundisha kuhusu mambo yote, nao ni kweli wala si uongo, na kama [upako huo] ulivyowafundisha, kaeni ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Kwa upande wenu, mlipokea upako kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, na upako huo unakaa ndani yenu; hamhitaji mtu yeyote awafundishe. Badala yake, upako {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} unawafundisha kuhusu kila kitu, nao ni kweli wala si uongo. Kwa hiyo, kama upako huo ulivyowafundisha, kaeni ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Lakini ninyi mlipokea upako kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, na upako huo unakaa ndani yenu. Kwa hiyo hamhitaji mtu yeyote awafundishe. Upako unaotoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} unawafundisha kuhusu kila kitu. Mafundisho hayo ni kweli, si uongo. Basi kaeni ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kama mlivyofundishwa.

decisions.choice: and you: the sentence starts with "you", then makes the anointing the subject
decisions.reason: ὑμεῖς is set at the head for emphasis, as in 2:20 and 2:24, but the clause continues with the anointing as subject.

decisions.choice: the anointing: as in 2:20, most likely the Holy Spirit, given by Christ
alternatives: God's word, the message they heard
decisions.reason: What is said here, that it remains in them and teaches them about everything, Jesus says of the Spirit (John 14:16-17, 14:26). See the note on 2:20. "From him" is the Holy One of 2:20, here most likely Christ, who comes in 2:28.

decisions.choice: no need for anyone to teach you: no need of the new teaching the deceivers offer
alternatives: no need of any human teacher at all
decisions.reason: John himself is teaching them in this letter, so he does not mean that teachers are useless. He means they need no one to add to what the anointing has taught them, least of all the deceivers of 2:26.

decisions.choice: remain in him: a command
alternatives: you remain in him: a statement of fact
decisions.reason: μένετε has the same form in the present indicative and the imperative. 2:28 repeats it plainly as a command, "And now ... remain in him", which favors a command here too; read as a statement it would be a word of assurance.

decisions.choice: in him: in Christ
decisions.reason: αὐτῷ could be neuter and refer to the anointing, but 2:28 goes on with "remain in him ... when he appears", which is Christ.

decisions.choice: the long sentence leads up to its main verb, remain
decisions.reason: After "but as" the sentence piles up three clauses about the anointing before it reaches the command, "remain in him".

decisions.choice: [the anointing] taught (L); the anointing has taught (B); you have been taught (R)
decisions.reason: The anointing is most likely the Spirit (meaning decision m2), and the translation does not call the Spirit "it". English repeats "the anointing" or uses a passive instead.

decisions.choice: the long sentence broken into shorter ones
decisions.reason: Balanced uses three sentences and Readable five, with the command at the end as in the Greek.

decisions.choice: selon qu’elle vous a enseignés (L); comme elle vous l’a enseigné (B); comme vous l’avez appris (R)
decisions.reason: The English repeats "the anointing" so as not to call the Spirit "it" (m2). French has no neuter: "elle" simply refers back to the feminine noun "onction", as it would for any noun, so Literal and Balanced use it without saying anything about the Spirit. Readable uses an active "vous l’avez appris" for the English passive.

source.text: Καὶ νῦν, τεκνία, μένετε ἐν αὐτῷ, ἵνα ἐὰν φανερωθῇ σχῶμεν παρρησίαν καὶ μὴ αἰσχυνθῶμεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And now, little children, remain in him, so that if he is revealed we may have boldness and not be put to shame from him at the coming of him.

en.L: And now, little children, remain in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} appears we may have boldness and not shrink in shame from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coming.
en.B: And now, dear children, remain in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} appears, we will be able to face {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} boldly at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coming, instead of turning away from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in shame.
en.R: And now, dear children, remain in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes back and appears, we can stand before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} boldly. We will not have to turn away from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in shame.

fr.L: Et maintenant, petits enfants, demeurez en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, afin que, quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} paraîtra, nous ayons de l’assurance et que nous ne nous détournions pas de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dans la honte, à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} venue.
fr.B: Et maintenant, mes chers enfants, demeurez en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Alors, quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} paraîtra, nous pourrons nous tenir devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} avec assurance à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} venue, au lieu de nous détourner de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} avec honte.
fr.R: Et maintenant, mes chers enfants, demeurez en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Alors, quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} reviendra et se montrera, nous pourrons nous tenir devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} avec assurance. Nous n’aurons pas à nous détourner de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} avec honte.

es.L: Y ahora, hijitos, {{plural_you:permanezcan|permaneced}} en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, para que, cuando se manifieste, tengamos confianza y no nos apartemos de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} avergonzados en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} venida.
es.B: Y ahora, hijitos, {{plural_you:permanezcan|permaneced}} en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Así, cuando se manifieste, podremos presentarnos ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} con confianza en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} venida, en lugar de apartarnos de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} avergonzados.
es.R: Y ahora, hijos queridos, {{plural_you:permanezcan|permaneced}} en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Así, cuando vuelva y se manifieste, podremos estar delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} sin miedo. No tendremos que apartarnos de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} avergonzados.

sw.L: Na sasa, watoto wadogo, kaeni ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, ili akidhihirishwa tuwe na uhuru, wala tusirudi nyuma mbali {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} kwa aibu wakati wa kuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.B: Na sasa, wanangu wapendwa, kaeni ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Ndipo atakapodhihirishwa, tutaweza kusimama mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa ujasiri wakati wa kuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, badala ya kuficha nyuso zetu kwa aibu.
sw.R: Na sasa, wanangu wapendwa, kaeni ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Ndipo, atakaporudi na kuonekana, tutaweza kusimama mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} bila hofu. Hatutalazimika kuficha nyuso zetu mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa aibu.

decisions.choice: when he appears: his appearing is certain; only its time is unknown
decisions.reason: ἐὰν can introduce something sure to happen whose time is not known (as in John 14:3). There is no doubt that he will appear.

decisions.choice: appears: Christ shown openly at his return
decisions.reason: φανερόω is used of his first coming in 1:2 and 3:5, and of his return here and in 3:2.

decisions.choice: boldness: the freedom of someone who can face the judge without fear
decisions.reason: παρρησία first meant freedom of speech. In this letter it is the confidence believers have before God (3:21; 5:14) and on the day of judgment (4:17).

decisions.choice: be ashamed before him: shrink away from him in shame
decisions.reason: With ἀπ the verb pictures drawing back from someone in disgrace.

decisions.choice: coming: Christ's arrival at the end of the age
decisions.reason: παρουσία means presence or arrival, and was used of a ruler's visit. It is the usual word for Christ's return (Matthew 24:3, 24:27; 1 Thessalonians 4:15), found only here in John's writings.

decisions.choice: we: John includes himself with his readers
alternatives: we, John and the other leaders, ashamed of those we taught
decisions.reason: He changes from "you" to "we". He may include himself as one who must also face Christ, or he may mean that he and the other leaders would be ashamed if their children fell away. The plain sense is the first.

decisions.choice: comes back and appears
decisions.reason: Readable says that the appearing is Christ's return (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: the purpose clause made a separate sentence
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable begin a new sentence with "Then".

decisions.choice: de l’assurance, avec assurance; à sa venue
decisions.reason: "Assurance" says the freedom of one who can face the judge without fear (m3) and is used again in 3:21, 4:17 and 5:14. "Venue" is the plain word for Christ's coming (m5); "avènement" is now mostly said of a king's accession.

decisions.choice: confianza (L, B); sin miedo (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1 John 5:14, where the same word is "confianza" at Balanced and "sin miedo" at Readable. Here Literal also says "confianza", because the picture is facing a judge (meaning decision m3), not speaking freely in prayer. "Venida" for his coming, as in the other letters.

decisions.choice: uhuru (L); kwa ujasiri (B); bila hofu (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:14: the word is the freedom of someone who can face the judge without fear (m3). Literal says "uhuru" (freedom), Balanced "ujasiri" (boldness), and Readable says what it means in practice, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: akidhihirishwa (L); atakapodhihirishwa (B); kuja kwake
decisions.reason: Christ shown openly at his return (m2): "kudhihirishwa" is the same verb used for the life that was revealed in 1:2. "Kuja" is the plain word for his coming (m5), as in the Gospels; Readable says "atakaporudi" (when he comes back), as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἐὰν εἰδῆτε ὅτι δίκαιός ἐστιν, γινώσκετε ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ποιῶν τὴν δικαιοσύνην ἐξ αὐτοῦ γεγέννηται.

records.literal_gloss: If you know that righteous he is, you know that everyone the [one] doing the righteousness from him has been born.

en.L: If you know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is righteous, you know that everyone who does righteousness has been born of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Since you know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is righteous, you can be sure that everyone who does what is righteous has been born of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: You know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is righteous. So you can also be sure that everyone who does what is right has been born of God.

fr.L: Si vous savez qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est juste, vous savez que quiconque pratique la justice est né de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Puisque vous savez qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est juste, vous pouvez être sûrs que quiconque fait ce qui est juste est né de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Vous savez qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est juste. Alors vous pouvez être sûrs aussi que celui qui fait ce qui est bien est né de Dieu.

es.L: Si {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es justo, {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que todo el que practica la justicia ha nacido de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Puesto que {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es justo, {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} estar seguros de que todo el que hace lo que es justo ha nacido de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes saben|Vosotros sabéis}} que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es justo. Así que también {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} estar seguros de que todo el que hace lo que es justo ha nacido de Dios.

sw.L: Ikiwa mnajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mwenye haki, mnajua kwamba kila anayetenda haki amezaliwa kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.B: Kwa kuwa mnajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mwenye haki, mnaweza kuwa na hakika kwamba kila anayetenda yaliyo ya haki amezaliwa {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.R: Mnajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mwenye haki. Kwa hiyo mnaweza pia kuwa na hakika kwamba kila anayetenda haki amezaliwa na Mungu.

decisions.choice: if you know: a premise the readers accept, so "since you know"
decisions.reason: ἐὰν here does not express doubt; John is building on what they already know.

decisions.choice: you know: a statement
decisions.reason: γινώσκετε could be an indicative or an imperative. The statement fits the reasoning best: if you know this, you also know that.

decisions.choice: he is righteous: probably Christ; born of him: God
decisions.reason: The nearest person is Christ (2:28), and he is called righteous in 2:1 and 3:7. But John never speaks of being born of Christ; every other time it is born of God (3:9; 4:7; 5:1, 5:4, 5:18; John 1:13), and 3:1 goes straight on to "children of God". John may move from Son to Father without marking it, or he may mean God throughout (God is called righteous in 1:9).

decisions.choice: doing what is righteous shows that a person has been born of God
alternatives: doing right is how one becomes born of God
decisions.reason: The perfect γεγέννηται puts the birth first; the doing of right, a continuing way of life (present tense), is the evidence of it, not the cause. This is the first mention of new birth in the letter.

decisions.choice: does what is righteous (B); does what is right (R)
decisions.reason: "Does righteousness" is not natural English. Balanced keeps the key term as "righteous"; Readable says "right", the everyday word for the same thing.

decisions.choice: born of God
decisions.reason: Readable names God, following meaning decision m3; Literal and Balanced keep "him".

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}; {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: Pronouns for God or Christ take the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: pratique la justice (L); fait ce qui est juste (B); fait ce qui est bien (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: "Faire la justice" would suggest administering justice. Literal keeps the noun "justice" of the term sheet with "pratiquer"; Balanced keeps the key word as "juste", and Readable uses the everyday "bien", as the English Readable says "right". Literal and Balanced say the same in 3:7 and 3:10, where Readable follows the English "live a righteous life" ("vivre d’une manière juste").

decisions.choice: kutenda haki; amezaliwa kutoka kwake (L), amezaliwa naye (B), amezaliwa na Mungu (R)
decisions.reason: "Haki" is the key word for righteousness, so Readable keeps it where the English Readable says "what is right" (m4). As in 5:1, Literal keeps the Greek "from" with "kutoka kwake", and Balanced and Readable use the passive with "na", the ordinary way to name who gave birth.
